sentences.zh: 列傳第二百二 文苑五

translations.literal: Biographies 202: The Literary Garden, Part Five.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 202: The Literary Garden, Part 5

sentences.zh: 梅堯臣 江休復 蘇洵 章望之 王逢 孫唐卿 黃庠 楊寘 附 唐庚 史伯虎附 文同 楊傑 賀鑄 劉涇 鮑由 黃伯思

translations.literal: Mei Yaochen, Jiang Xiufu, Su Xun, Zhang Wangzhi, Wang Feng, Sun Tangqing, Huang Xiang, Yang Zhi — with appended: Tang Geng, Shi Bohu (appended), Wen Tong, Yang Jie, He Zhu, Liu Jing, Bao You, Huang Bosi.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Yaochen, Jiang Xiufu, Su Xun, Zhang Wangzhi, Wang Feng, Sun Tangqing, Huang Xiang, and Yang Zhi; appended biographies: Tang Geng, Shi Bohu, Wen Tong, Yang Jie, He Zhu, Liu Jing, Bao You, and Huang Bosi.

sentences.zh: 梅堯臣，字聖俞，宣州宣城人，侍讀學士詢從子也。

translations.literal: Mei Yaochen, styled Shengyu, was a man of Xuancheng in Xuanzhou, a nephew by descent of Academician Reader Mei Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Yaochen, courtesy name Shengyu, was from Xuancheng in Xuanzhou and was a nephew of the Academician Reader Mei Xun.

sentences.zh: 工為詩，以深遠古淡為意，間出奇巧，初未為人所知。

translations.literal: He was skilled at composing poetry, aiming at depth, remoteness, antiquity, and plainness, occasionally producing striking originality; at first he was not known to people.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at poetry, aiming for depth, remoteness, antiquity, and restraint, with occasional flashes of striking originality; at first he was little known.

sentences.zh: 用詢陰為河南主簿，錢惟演留守西京，特嗟賞之，為忘年交，引與酬倡，一府盡傾。

translations.literal: Through Xun's private recommendation he became Registrar of Henan; Qian Weiyan, holding the western capital in garrison, especially admired and sighed over him, made a friendship across generations, drew him into reciprocal composition, and the whole prefectural staff was won over.
translations.idiomatic: Through Xun's quiet recommendation he was appointed Registrar of Henan. Qian Weiyan, who was holding the western capital, took a special liking to him, became his friend despite the age gap, brought him into literary exchange, and won over the entire prefectural staff.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修與為詩友，自以為不及。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu became his poetic companion and considered himself not equal to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu became his poetic companion and considered himself inferior to him.

sentences.zh: 堯臣益刻厲，精思苦學，繇是知名於時。

translations.literal: Yaochen became all the more exacting, with refined thought and bitter study; thereby he became known in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Yaochen redoubled his discipline, thinking deeply and studying hard, and thereby made a name for himself.

sentences.zh: 宋興，以詩名家為世所傳如堯臣者，蓋少也。

translations.literal: Since the rise of Song, those who made a family name in poetry and were transmitted by the age like Yaochen were perhaps few.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of the Song, few poets of Yaochen's stature have been so widely read.

sentences.zh: 嘗語人曰：「凡詩，意新語工，得前人所未道者，斯為善矣。

translations.literal: He once told people: "As for all poetry, when the idea is fresh and the language is crafted, attaining what predecessors have not expressed — that is what is good.
translations.idiomatic: He once said to others, "In poetry, what is good is an idea that is fresh and language that is finely wrought, expressing what no predecessor has yet said.

sentences.zh: 必能狀難寫之景如在目前，含不盡之意見於言外，然後為至也。」

translations.literal: One must be able to depict scenes hard to write as if before the eyes, and contain inexhaustible meaning seen beyond the words — only then is it ultimate."
translations.idiomatic: One must be able to render scenes that are hard to capture as if they were before one's eyes, and to suggest inexhaustible meaning beyond the words — only then has one reached the highest level."

sentences.zh: 世以為知言。

translations.literal: The age considered this knowledgeable speech.
translations.idiomatic: The world regarded this as the speech of one who truly understood the art.

sentences.zh: 歷德興縣令，知建德、襄城縣，監湖州稅，簽書忠武、鎮安判官，監永豐倉。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Dexing, administered Jiande and Xiangcheng counties, supervised the tax of Huzhou, signed as judicial administrator of Zhongwu and Zhen'an, and supervised the Yongfeng granary.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Dexing, as prefect of Jiande and Xiangcheng, as supervisor of Huzhou tax collection, as signing judicial administrator for Zhongwu and Zhen'an, and as supervisor of the Yongfeng granary.

sentences.zh: 大臣屢薦宜在館閣，召試，賜進士出身，為國子監直講，累遷尚書都官員外郎。

translations.literal: Great ministers repeatedly recommended that he should be in the academies; he was summoned for examination, granted jinshi origin, made Direct Lecturer of the Directorate of Education, and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers repeatedly recommended him for service in the academies. Summoned for examination, he was granted jinshi standing, appointed Direct Lecturer of the Directorate of Education, and eventually promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 預修《唐書》，成，未奏而卒，錄其子一人。

translations.literal: He took part in compiling the History of Tang; when it was completed he died before presenting it, and one son was recorded for favor.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in compiling the History of Tang. When the work was finished he died before it could be submitted to the throne, and one of his sons was granted an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 寶元、嘉祐中，仁宗有事郊廟，堯臣預祭，輒獻歌詩，又嘗上書言兵。

translations.literal: In the Baoyuan and Jiayou periods, when Renzong had affairs at the suburban altars and temples, Yaochen participated in the sacrifices and always presented songs and poems; he also once submitted a memorial on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoyuan and Jiayou reign periods, whenever Emperor Renzong performed suburban sacrifices, Yaochen took part in the rites and presented celebratory poems. He also once submitted a memorial on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 注《孫子》十三篇，撰《唐載記》二十六卷、《毛詩小傳》二十卷、《宛陵集》四十卷。

translations.literal: He annotated the thirteen chapters of Sunzi, and composed Records of Tang in twenty-six juan, Small Commentary on the Mao Odes in twenty juan, and the Wanling Collection in forty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He annotated the thirteen chapters of Sunzi and wrote Records of Tang in twenty-six juan, a Small Commentary on the Mao Odes in twenty juan, and the Wanling Collection in forty juan.

sentences.zh: 堯臣家貧，喜飲酒，賢士大夫多從之遊，時載酒過門。

translations.literal: Yaochen's family was poor; he delighted in drinking wine, and many worthy scholar-officials followed him in travel, at times carrying wine to his door.
translations.idiomatic: Yaochen's family was poor. He loved wine, and many worthy scholar-officials sought his company, often arriving at his door with wine in hand.

sentences.zh: 善談笑，與物無忤，詼嘲刺譏托於詩，晚益工。

translations.literal: He was skilled at jest and laughter, at odds with nothing, and placed witty mockery and satirical barbs in his poetry; in his later years he became all the more accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: He was witty and easygoing, offended no one, and embedded humor and satire in his verse, which grew more accomplished in his later years.

sentences.zh: 有人得西南夷布弓衣，其織文乃堯臣詩也，名重於時如此。

translations.literal: Someone obtained a bowman's garment of southwestern barbarian cloth, and its woven pattern was Yaochen's poetry — such was his fame in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Someone obtained a bowman's jacket of southwestern tribal cloth whose woven pattern turned out to be one of Yaochen's poems — such was his renown.

sentences.zh: 江休復，字鄰幾，開封陳留人。

translations.literal: Jiang Xiufu, styled Linji, was a man of Chenliu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xiufu, courtesy name Linji, was from Chenliu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 少強學博覽，為文淳雅，尤善於詩。

translations.literal: In youth he studied strenuously and read broadly; his writing was pure and elegant, and he was especially skilled in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he studied hard and read widely. His prose was pure and elegant, and he was especially accomplished in poetry.

sentences.zh: 喜琴、弈、飲酒，不以聲利為意。

translations.literal: He delighted in the zither, chess, and drinking wine, and did not take sound and profit as his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the zither, chess, and wine, and cared nothing for fame or gain.

sentences.zh: 進士起家，為桂陽監藍山尉，騎驢之官，每據鞍讀書至迷失道，家人求得之。

translations.literal: Rising from the jinshi, he became Assistant Magistrate of Lanshan under the Lanshan salt monopoly of Guiyang, riding a donkey to his post; each time he leaned on the saddle reading until he lost the road, and his family had to find him.
translations.idiomatic: Having entered office through the jinshi examination, he was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Lanshan under the Guiyang salt monopoly. He rode a donkey to his post, often reading in the saddle until he lost his way and had to be fetched home by his family.

sentences.zh: 舉書判拔萃，改大理寺丞，遷殿中丞。

translations.literal: He was nominated for outstanding legal judgment, was changed to Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review, and was promoted to Director in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Nominated for outstanding performance in legal judgments, he was promoted to Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review and then to Director in the Palace.

sentences.zh: 獻其所著書，召試，為集賢校理，判尚書刑部。

translations.literal: He presented the books he had written, was summoned for examination, and became Collator of the Hall of Assembled Talents, with concurrent duty in the Ministry of Justice of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After presenting his writings and passing a palace examination, he was appointed Collator in the Hall of Assembled Talents with concurrent duty in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 與蘇舜欽遊，坐預進奏院祠神會落職，監蔡州商稅。

translations.literal: He associated with Su Shunqin and, on account of taking part in the Spirit Sacrifice gathering of the Memorial Submission Court, was removed from office and supervised the commercial tax of Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had associated with Su Shunqin and took part in the Spirit Sacrifice gathering at the Memorial Submission Court, he was dismissed from office and appointed supervisor of commercial tax in Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，知奉符縣，通判睦州，徙廬州，復集賢校理，判吏部南曹、登聞鼓院，為群牧判官，出知同州，提點陝西路刑獄，入判三司鹽鐵勾院，修起居注，累遷尚書刑部郎中，卒。

translations.literal: After a long time he administered Fengfu County, served as deputy prefect of Muzhou, was transferred to Luzhou, was again Collator of the Hall of Assembled Talents, judged the Southern Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel and the Court of Complaints and Appeals, was judicial administrator of the Pasturage Commission, went out to administer Tongzhou, was Investigating Commissioner for criminal justice on the Shaanxi circuit, entered to judge the Audit Office of the Salt and Iron Commission of the Three Offices, compiled the Imperial Diary, was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Justice of the Department of State Affairs, and died.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he served as magistrate of Fengfu, as deputy prefect of Muzhou, and then of Luzhou. He was reappointed Collator in the Hall of Assembled Talents, served in the Southern Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel and the Court of Complaints and Appeals, and as judicial administrator of the Pasturage Commission. He later governed Tongzhou, served as Investigating Commissioner for criminal justice on the Shaanxi circuit, and entered the capital to judge the Salt and Iron Commission's audit office and compile the Imperial Diary. He rose to Director in the Ministry of Justice and died in office.

sentences.zh: 休復外簡曠而內行甚飾，事孀姑如母，所與遊皆一時豪俊。

translations.literal: Xiufu was outwardly simple and expansive while his inner conduct was greatly adorned; he served his widowed aunt as a mother, and those with whom he associated were all heroic talents of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly Xiufu was plain and unassuming, yet inwardly his conduct was meticulous. He treated his widowed aunt as his own mother, and his companions were the leading talents of the day.

sentences.zh: 為政簡易。

translations.literal: In governing he was simple and easy.
translations.idiomatic: In office his administration was simple and unobtrusive.

sentences.zh: 嘗著《神告》一篇，言皇嗣未立，假神告祖宗之意，冀以感悟。

translations.literal: He once wrote a piece called Divine Admonition, saying the imperial heir had not been established, borrowing the idea of the spirits admonishing the ancestors, hoping thereby to awaken understanding.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote a piece called Divine Admonition, arguing that no heir apparent had been named and invoking, through a supposed divine message to the imperial ancestors, the hope of moving the court to act.

sentences.zh: 又嘗言昭憲太后子孫多流落民間，宜甄錄之。

translations.literal: He also once said that many descendants of Empress Dowager Zhaoxian had drifted among the common people and ought to be selected and recorded.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that many descendants of Empress Dowager Zhaoxian had been scattered among the people and ought to be identified and given official recognition.

sentences.zh: 著《唐宜鑒》十五卷、《春秋世論》三十卷、文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He wrote Mirror of Tang Institutions in fifteen juan, Discussions of the Ages in the Spring and Autumn Annals in thirty juan, and a collection of writings in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His works included Mirror of Tang Institutions in fifteen juan, Discussions of the Ages in the Spring and Autumn Annals in thirty juan, and a collection of writings in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 蘇洵，字明允，眉州眉山人。

translations.literal: Su Xun, styled Mingyun, was a man of Meishan in Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Su Xun, courtesy name Mingyun, was from Meishan in Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 年二十七始發憤為學，歲餘舉進士，又舉茂才異等，皆不中。

translations.literal: At age twenty-seven he first roused himself in indignation to study; within a year he presented himself for the jinshi and also for Outstanding Talent with Special Qualifications — in neither did he pass.
translations.idiomatic: Not until he was twenty-seven did he throw himself into study with fierce resolve. A little more than a year later he took the jinshi examination and also presented himself for Outstanding Talent with Special Qualifications, but failed both.

sentences.zh: 悉焚常所為文，閉戶益讀書，遂通《六經》、百家之說，下筆頃刻數千言。

translations.literal: He burned all the writings he had ordinarily made, shut his door and read all the more, and thereby mastered the Six Classics and the teachings of the hundred schools; when he put brush to paper, in an instant there were several thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: He burned all his earlier writings, shut himself in, and read still harder until he had mastered the Six Classics and the teachings of the hundred schools. When he wrote, thousands of words flowed from his brush in moments.

sentences.zh: 至和、嘉祐間，與其二子軾、轍皆至京師，翰林學士歐陽修上其所著書二十二篇，既出，士大夫爭傳之，一時學者競效蘇氏為文章。

translations.literal: Between the Zhihe and Jiayou periods, he and his two sons Shi and Zhe all reached the capital; Hanlin Academician Ouyang Xiu presented his twenty-two written pieces; once they appeared, scholar-officials vied to transmit them, and for a time students all raced to imitate the Su family in composition.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhihe and Jiayou reign periods he and his two sons Shi and Zhe all came to the capital. Hanlin Academician Ouyang Xiu presented twenty-two of his essays to the throne. Once they circulated, scholar-officials passed them around eagerly, and students everywhere rushed to imitate the Su style.

sentences.zh: 所著《權書》、《衡論》、《機策》，文多不可悉錄，錄其《心術》、《遠慮》二篇。

translations.literal: Among his writings, The Book of Expediency, Discourses on Balance, and Stratagems — most of the texts cannot all be recorded; two pieces are recorded here: Heart Technique and Far-Sighted Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Among his works, The Book of Expediency, Discourses on Balance, and Stratagems contain far more than can be quoted in full. Two essays are recorded here: Heart Technique and Far-Sighted Counsel.

sentences.zh: 《心術》曰：

translations.literal: Heart Technique says:
translations.idiomatic: Heart Technique reads:

sentences.zh: 為將之道，當先治心，太山覆於前而色不變，麋鹿興於左而目不瞬，然後可以待敵。

translations.literal: The way of being a general: one should first govern the heart — when Mount Tai collapses before one the complexion does not change, when a stag rises on the left the eye does not blink; only then can one await the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The way of command is to master the mind first: let Mount Tai collapse before you without a change of expression, let a stag spring up at your left without a blink of the eye — only then are you fit to face the enemy.

sentences.zh: 凡兵上義，不義雖利不動。

translations.literal: In all warfare righteousness is paramount; if unrighteous, though there be profit one does not move.
translations.idiomatic: In warfare righteousness comes first: if a cause is unjust, do not act even when gain is at hand.

sentences.zh: 夫惟義可以怒士，士以義怒，可與百戰。

translations.literal: Only righteousness can rouse the soldiers; when soldiers are roused by righteousness, they can fight a hundred battles.
translations.idiomatic: Only righteousness can stir soldiers to fury; soldiers roused by righteousness will fight through a hundred battles.

sentences.zh: 凡戰之道，未戰養其財，將戰養其力，既戰養其氣，既勝養其心。

translations.literal: The way of all warfare: before battle nurture their resources; on the verge of battle nurture their strength; after battle has begun nurture their spirit; after victory nurture their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The art of war is this: before battle, nurture your resources; as battle approaches, nurture your strength; once fighting has begun, nurture your morale; after victory, nurture your men's resolve.

sentences.zh: 謹烽燧，嚴斥堠，使耕者無所顧忌，所以養其財，豐犒而優遊之，所以養其力。

translations.literal: Be strict with beacon fires and watch-towers, make farmers without apprehension — thereby nurturing their resources; give rich rewards and let them move at ease — thereby nurturing their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Keep beacon fires and watch-towers in good order so farmers may work without fear — that is how you nurture your resources. Reward your men generously and let them rest at ease — that is how you nurture their strength.

sentences.zh: 小勝益急，小挫益厲，所以養其氣。

translations.literal: Small victories make them all the more urgent, small setbacks make them all the more stern — thereby nurturing their spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Small victories should spur them on; small setbacks should steel them — that is how you nurture their fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 用人不盡其所為，所以養其心。

translations.literal: Employ men without exhausting what they can do — thereby nurturing their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Do not use your men to the limit of what they can give — that is how you nurture their hearts.

sentences.zh: 故士當蓄其怒、懷其欲而不盡。

translations.literal: Therefore soldiers should store their anger and harbor their desires without exhausting them.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers should therefore keep anger banked and desire held in reserve, never fully spent.

sentences.zh: 怒不盡則有餘勇，欲不盡則有餘貪，故雖並天下而士不厭兵，此黃帝所以七十戰而兵不殆也。

translations.literal: When anger is not exhausted there is surplus courage; when desire is not exhausted there is surplus craving — thus even though uniting the realm, the soldiers do not weary of war; this is why the Yellow Emperor fought seventy battles yet his troops did not fail.
translations.idiomatic: Unspent anger leaves courage in reserve; unspent desire leaves hunger for more. Thus even after conquering the realm, soldiers do not tire of war. That is why the Yellow Emperor fought seventy battles without his army wearing out.

sentences.zh: 凡將欲智而嚴，凡士欲愚。

translations.literal: All generals should wish to be wise and stern; all soldiers should wish to be foolish.
translations.idiomatic: Generals must be wise and stern; soldiers must be kept simple.

sentences.zh: 智則不可測，嚴則不可犯，故士皆委己而聽命，夫安得不愚？

translations.literal: Wise, then they cannot be fathomed; stern, then they cannot be violated — therefore soldiers all entrust themselves and heed orders; how could they not be foolish?
translations.idiomatic: If a commander is wise he cannot be fathomed; if he is stern he cannot be defied. Soldiers therefore surrender themselves to his orders — how could they not seem foolish?

sentences.zh: 夫惟士愚而後可與之皆死。

translations.literal: Only when soldiers are foolish can one die with them all.
translations.idiomatic: Only when soldiers are kept simple can a commander ask them all to die together with him.

sentences.zh: 凡兵之動，知敵之主，知敵之將，而後可以動於嶮。

translations.literal: In all movement of troops, know the enemy's lord, know the enemy's general — only then can one move in danger.
translations.idiomatic: Before moving troops into peril, know the enemy's sovereign and know the enemy's commander.

sentences.zh: 鄧艾縋兵於穴中，非劉禪之庸，則百萬之師可以坐縛，彼固有所侮而動也。

translations.literal: Deng Ai lowered troops by rope into a cavern — had it not been for Liu Shan's mediocrity, a force of a million could have been bound while seated; they certainly had something to despise before they moved.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Ai lowered his men into the mountain passes by rope, had Liu Shan not been so inept, a million-man army could have been captured without a fight. He moved because he knew precisely whom he could despise.

sentences.zh: 故古之賢將，能以兵嘗敵，而又以敵自嘗，故去就可以決。

translations.literal: Therefore the worthy generals of antiquity could use troops to test the enemy, and also use the enemy to test themselves — thus advance and retreat could be decided.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient worthy commanders therefore tested the enemy with their troops and tested themselves against the enemy, so that advance and retreat could be decided with confidence.

sentences.zh: 凡主將之道，知理而後可以舉兵，知勢而後可以加兵，知節而後可以用兵。

translations.literal: The way of all commanding generals: know principle and then one can raise troops; know momentum and then one can add troops; know measure and then one can employ troops.
translations.idiomatic: The commander-in-chief must understand principle before he may raise an army, understand momentum before he may reinforce it, and understand measure before he may deploy it.

sentences.zh: 知理則不屈，知勢則不沮，知節則不窮。

translations.literal: Knowing principle, one is not bent; knowing momentum, one is not discouraged; knowing measure, one is not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Understanding principle, he will not be broken; understanding momentum, he will not lose heart; understanding measure, he will not be spent.

sentences.zh: 見小利不動，見小患不遷，小利小患不足以辱吾技也，夫然後有以支大利大患。

translations.literal: Seeing small profit one does not move; seeing small trouble one does not shift — small profit and small trouble are insufficient to insult our skill; only then is there means to sustain great profit and great trouble.
translations.idiomatic: He does not stir at small gains or shift at small troubles, for petty stakes are unworthy of his skill. Only then can he bear up under great stakes and great crises.

sentences.zh: 夫惟養技而自愛者無敵於天下，故一忍可以支百勇，一靜可以制百動。

translations.literal: Only one who nurtures skill and cherishes himself is without enemy under Heaven; thus one forbearance can sustain a hundred courages, one stillness can restrain a hundred movements.
translations.idiomatic: Only one who cultivates his skill and guards his strength is unmatched under Heaven. One act of forbearance can withstand a hundred displays of courage; one stillness can master a hundred movements.

sentences.zh: 兵有長短，敵我一也。

translations.literal: Troops have strengths and weaknesses; enemy and self are one.
translations.idiomatic: Armies have strengths and weaknesses on both sides alike.

sentences.zh: 敢問：「吾之所長，吾出而用之，彼將不與吾校；

translations.literal: I dare ask: "Where we are strong, if we bring it forth and use it, they will not contend with us;
translations.idiomatic: One may ask: "Where we are strong, if we bring our strength out and use it, the enemy will not contest us;

sentences.zh: 吾之所短，吾斂而置之，彼將強與吾角。

translations.literal: where we are weak, if we gather it in and set it aside, they will forcefully contend with us.
translations.idiomatic: but where we are weak, if we gather our weakness in and set it aside, they will press hard to fight us on that ground.

sentences.zh: 奈何？」

translations.literal: What then?"
translations.idiomatic: What is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「吾之所短，吾抗而暴之，使之疑而卻；

translations.literal: It is said: "Where we are weak, we resist and expose it, making them doubtful and causing them to withdraw;
translations.idiomatic: The answer: "Where we are weak, we confront it openly and display it boldly, making the enemy doubtful and causing him to pull back;

sentences.zh: 吾之所長，吾陰而養之，使之狎而墮其中。

translations.literal: where we are strong, we conceal and nurture it, making them familiar until they fall within it.
translations.idiomatic: where we are strong, we hide and cultivate it, until the enemy grows familiar with us and falls into the trap.

sentences.zh: 此用長短之術也。」

translations.literal: This is the technique of employing strengths and weaknesses."
translations.idiomatic: That is the art of turning strength and weakness to account."

sentences.zh: 善用兵者使之無所顧，有所恃。

translations.literal: One who is skilled at employing troops makes them without anything to look back to, yet with something to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: A skilled commander leaves his men with nothing to fall back on, yet something to rely upon.

sentences.zh: 無所顧則知死之不足惜，有所恃則知不至於必敗。

translations.literal: With nothing to look back to, they know death is not worth sparing; with something to rely on, they know they will not necessarily be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: With nothing to fall back on, they know death is not too dear; with something to rely on, they know defeat is not inevitable.

sentences.zh: 尺箠當猛虎，奮呼而操擊，徒手遇蜥蜴，變色而卻步，人之情也，知此者可以將矣。

translations.literal: With a foot-rule whip facing a fierce tiger, one shouts and strikes; bare-handed meeting a lizard, one's color changes and one steps back — such is human feeling; knowing this, one can command troops.
translations.idiomatic: A man will shout and strike with a foot-rule whip at a tiger, yet blanch and step back when he meets a lizard bare-handed — such is human nature. One who understands this may command armies.

sentences.zh: 袒裼而按劍，則烏獲不敢逼；

translations.literal: Bare-chested with hand on sword, then Wuyou dare not press close;
translations.idiomatic: Bare-chested with hand on the sword, even Wuyou would not dare approach;

sentences.zh: 冠冑衣甲據兵而寢，則童子彎弓殺之矣。

translations.literal: crowned, armored, clothed in mail, holding weapons yet sleeping, then a boy bending a bow can kill him.
translations.idiomatic: but crowned, armored, and sleeping with weapons in hand, a child bending a bow could kill him.

sentences.zh: 故善用兵者以形固，夫能以形固，則力有餘矣。

translations.literal: Therefore one skilled at employing troops fixes them by form; if one can fix them by form, then strength has surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the skilled commander fixes his men's strength through posture and bearing. When form is firm, force remains in reserve.

sentences.zh: 《遠慮》曰：

translations.literal: Far-Sighted Counsel says:
translations.idiomatic: Far-Sighted Counsel reads:

sentences.zh: 聖人之道，有經、有權、有機，是以有民、有群臣而又有腹心之臣。

translations.literal: The way of the sage has constants, expedients, and stratagems — therefore there are the people, there are the many ministers, and again there are heart-and-belly ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The way of the sage rests on constants, expedients, and secret stratagems. Hence there are the people, the many ministers, and also ministers of the innermost counsel.

sentences.zh: 曰經者，天下之民舉知之可也；

translations.literal: What is called constant: all the people under Heaven may together know it;
translations.idiomatic: What is constant may be known to all the people under Heaven;

sentences.zh: 曰權者，民不可得而知矣，群臣知之可也；

translations.literal: what is called expedient: the people cannot obtain knowledge of it — the many ministers may know it;
translations.idiomatic: what is expedient cannot be known to the people, though the many ministers may know it;

sentences.zh: 曰機者，雖群臣亦不得而知之矣，腹心之臣知之可也。

translations.literal: what is called stratagem: even the many ministers likewise cannot obtain knowledge of it — heart-and-belly ministers may know it.
translations.idiomatic: what is stratagem cannot be known even to the many ministers — only ministers of the innermost counsel may know it.

sentences.zh: 夫使聖人無權，則無以成天下之務，無機，則無以濟萬世之功，然皆非天下之民所宜知；

translations.literal: If the sage had no expedients, then there would be no means to accomplish the affairs of the realm; without stratagems, no means to complete the achievements of ten thousand generations — yet none of these are what the people under Heaven ought to know;
translations.idiomatic: Without expedients the sage could not accomplish the affairs of the realm; without stratagems he could not secure achievements for ten thousand generations — yet neither is fit knowledge for the people.

sentences.zh: 而機者又群臣所不得聞，群臣不得聞，則誰與議？

translations.literal: and stratagems are again what the many ministers may not hear; if the many ministers may not hear, then with whom is one to deliberate?
translations.idiomatic: Stratagems, moreover, are what the many ministers must not hear. If ministers cannot hear them, with whom shall the sage deliberate?

sentences.zh: 不議不濟，然則所謂腹心之臣者，不可一日無也。

translations.literal: Without deliberation there is no completion — thus what are called heart-and-belly ministers cannot be absent for a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Without deliberation nothing is accomplished. Ministers of the innermost counsel therefore cannot be dispensed with even for a day.

sentences.zh: 後世見三代取天下以仁義，而守之以禮樂也，則曰「聖人無機」。

translations.literal: Later ages, seeing the Three Dynasties take the realm by benevolence and righteousness and guard it by rites and music, then say "the sage has no stratagems."
translations.idiomatic: Later ages, seeing that the Three Dynasties won the realm through benevolence and righteousness and kept it through rites and music, concluded that "the sage has no stratagems."

sentences.zh: 夫取天下與守天下，無機不能。

translations.literal: In taking the realm and in guarding the realm, without stratagems it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Neither winning the realm nor keeping it can be done without stratagems.

sentences.zh: 顧三代聖人之機，不若後世之詐，故後世不得見。

translations.literal: Only the stratagems of the sages of the Three Dynasties are not like the deceit of later ages — therefore later ages could not see them.
translations.idiomatic: But the stratagems of the Three Dynasties sages were unlike the deceit of later ages, and so later ages never perceived them.

sentences.zh: 其有機也，是以有腹心之臣。

translations.literal: Because they had stratagems, therefore they had heart-and-belly ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Because they had stratagems, they needed ministers of the innermost counsel.

sentences.zh: 禹有益，湯有伊尹，武王有太公望，是三臣者，聞天下之所不聞，知群臣之所不知。

translations.literal: Yu had Yi, Tang had Yi Yin, King Wu had Taigong Wang — these three ministers heard what all under Heaven did not hear and knew what the many ministers did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had Yi, Tang had Yi Yin, and King Wu had Taigong Wang. These three ministers heard what the world did not hear and knew what the many ministers did not know.

sentences.zh: 禹與湯武倡其機於上，而三臣者和之於下，以成萬世之功。

translations.literal: Yu and Tang and Wu initiated their stratagems above, while the three ministers harmonized below, thereby completing achievements for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, Tang, and Wu proclaimed their stratagems from above, and the three ministers harmonized them below, thereby securing achievements for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 下而至於桓、文，有管仲、狐偃為之謀主，闔廬有伍員，勾踐有范蠡、大夫種。

translations.literal: Descending to Duke Huan and Duke Wen, there were Guan Zhong and Hu Yan as their strategists; Helü had Wu Yuan; Goujian had Fan Li and Grandee Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Later came Duke Huan and Duke Wen, with Guan Zhong and Hu Yan as their chief strategists; King Helü had Wu Zixu; King Goujian had Fan Li and Grandee Zhong.

sentences.zh: 高祖之起也，大將任韓信、黥布、彭越，裨將任曹參、樊噲、滕公、灌嬰，遊說諸侯任酈生、陸賈、樅公，至於奇機密謀，君臣所不與者，唯留侯、酇侯二人。

translations.literal: When Gaozu rose, great generals were entrusted to Han Xin, Qing Bu, and Peng Yue; lieutenant generals to Cao Shen, Fan Kuai, the Lord of Teng, and Guan Ying; persuading the feudal lords to Li Yiji, Lu Jia, and the Lord of Zong — as for marvelous stratagems and secret plots in which ruler and ministers did not share, only the Marquis of Liu and the Marquis of Zan.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu rose, he entrusted his great generals to Han Xin, Qing Bu, and Peng Yue; his lieutenant generals to Cao Shen, Fan Kuai, the Lord of Teng, and Guan Ying; and his envoys to the feudal lords to Li Yiji, Lu Jia, and the Lord of Zong. But for marvelous stratagems and secret plots shared only between sovereign and minister, there were only the Marquis of Liu and the Marquis of Zan.

sentences.zh: 唐太宗之臣多奇才，而委之深、任之密者，亦不過曰房、杜。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong of Tang had many extraordinary ministers, yet those to whom he entrusted deeply and employed closely were also no more than Fang and Du.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong of Tang had many extraordinary ministers, yet those he entrusted most deeply were none other than Fang and Du.

sentences.zh: 夫君子為善之心與小人為惡之心一也，君子有機以成其善，小人有機以成其惡。

translations.literal: The heart of the gentleman in doing good and the heart of the petty man in doing evil are one; the gentleman has stratagems to complete his good, the petty man has stratagems to complete his evil.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman's desire to do good and the petty man's desire to do evil spring from the same impulse. The gentleman uses stratagems to accomplish good; the petty man uses stratagems to accomplish evil.

sentences.zh: 有機也，雖惡亦或濟，無機也，雖善亦不克，是故腹心之臣不可以一日無也。

translations.literal: With stratagems, even evil may sometimes succeed; without stratagems, even good cannot overcome — therefore heart-and-belly ministers cannot be absent for a single day.
translations.idiomatic: With stratagems, even evil may sometimes succeed; without stratagems, even good may fail. Ministers of the innermost counsel therefore cannot be dispensed with even for a day.

sentences.zh: 司馬氏，魏之賊也，有賈充之徒為之腹心之臣以濟，陳勝、吳廣，秦民之湯、武也，無腹心之臣以不克。

translations.literal: The Sima clan were the rebels of Wei; they had Jia Chong and his kind as heart-and-belly ministers and thereby succeeded. Chen Sheng and Wu Guang were the Tang and Wu of the Qin people, yet without heart-and-belly ministers they could not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: The Sima clan were usurpers of Wei, yet with Jia Chong and his like as ministers of innermost counsel they succeeded. Chen Sheng and Wu Guang were the Tang and Wu of the Qin people, yet without such ministers they failed.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 無腹心之臣，無機也，有機而洩也。

translations.literal: Without heart-and-belly ministers, there are no stratagems; with stratagems yet leaked.
translations.idiomatic: Without ministers of innermost counsel there are no stratagems; with stratagems that leak, there is failure.

sentences.zh: 夫無機與有機而洩者，譬如虎豹食人而不知設陷阱，設陷阱而不知以物覆其上者也。

translations.literal: Being without stratagems and having stratagems yet leaked are like a tiger or leopard eating people yet not knowing to set a trap, or setting a trap yet not knowing to cover it with something above.
translations.idiomatic: To lack stratagems or to have stratagems that leak is like a tiger that devours men yet does not know how to set a trap, or sets a trap yet does not know to cover it.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「機者，創業之君所假以濟耳，守成之世，其奚事機而安用夫腹心之臣？」

translations.literal: Someone said: "Stratagems are what founding rulers borrow to succeed — in ages that guard what is accomplished, what business have stratagems, and why employ heart-and-belly ministers?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone objected: "Stratagems are tools for founding rulers alone. In an age that merely preserves what has been won, what need is there for stratagems or for ministers of innermost counsel?"

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 守成之世，能遂熙然如太古之世矣乎？

translations.literal: In an age that guards what is accomplished, can it indeed be as tranquil and bright as the age of utmost antiquity?
translations.idiomatic: Can an age that merely preserves order truly be as tranquil as the age of utmost antiquity?

sentences.zh: 未也，吾未見機之可去也。

translations.literal: It is not so; I have not seen that stratagems can be removed.
translations.idiomatic: It is not so. I have never seen a time when stratagems could be dispensed with.

sentences.zh: 且夫天下之變，常伏於安，田文所謂「子少國危，大臣未附」，當是之時，而無腹心之臣，可為寒心哉！

translations.literal: Moreover, the changes of all under Heaven constantly lie hidden in security; what Tian Wen called "the son is young, the state is perilous, great ministers are not yet attached" — at such a time, without heart-and-belly ministers, how chilling to the heart!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, upheavals in the realm often lurk beneath apparent security. As Tian Wen said, "The heir is young, the state is in peril, and great ministers are not yet loyal." At such a moment, to lack ministers of innermost counsel is cause for dread.

sentences.zh: 昔者高祖之末，天下既定矣，而又以周勃遺孝惠、孝文；

translations.literal: In former times, at the end of Gaozu's reign, all under Heaven was already settled, yet he again bequeathed Zhou Bo to Emperor Xiaohui and Emperor Xiaowen;
translations.idiomatic: In former times, at the end of Gaozu's reign, when the realm was already settled, he still left Zhou Bo to Emperor Xiaohui and Emperor Xiaowen;

sentences.zh: 武帝之末，天下既治矣，而又以霍光遺孝昭、孝宣。

translations.literal: at the end of Emperor Wu's reign, all under Heaven was already governed, yet he again bequeathed Huo Guang to Emperor Xiaozhao and Emperor Xiaoxuan.
translations.idiomatic: and at the end of Emperor Wu's reign, when the realm was already well governed, he still left Huo Guang to Emperor Xiaozhao and Emperor Xiaoxuan.

sentences.zh: 蓋天下雖有泰山之勢，而聖人常以累卵為心，故雖守成之世，而腹心之臣不可去也。

translations.literal: For though all under Heaven has the momentum of Mount Tai, the sage constantly takes piled eggs as his heart — therefore even in ages that guard what is accomplished, heart-and-belly ministers cannot be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Though the realm may stand firm as Mount Tai, the sage always treats it as fragile as a pile of eggs. That is why ministers of innermost counsel cannot be dispensed with even in an age of settled order.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「百官總己以聽於塚宰。」

translations.literal: The Documents say: "The hundred officials gather themselves to heed the Grand Steward."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say, "The hundred officials gather themselves to heed the Grand Steward."

sentences.zh: 彼塚宰者，非腹心之臣，天子安能舉天下之事委之，三年不置疑於其間邪？

translations.literal: That Grand Steward — if not a heart-and-belly minister, how could the Son of Heaven entrust him with all affairs under Heaven and for three years harbor no doubt in the interval?
translations.idiomatic: That Grand Steward — if he were not a minister of innermost counsel, how could the Son of Heaven entrust him with all the affairs of the realm and go three years without a flicker of doubt?

sentences.zh: 又曰：「五載一巡狩。」

translations.literal: It also says: "Every five years, one imperial tour of inspection."
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "Every five years the ruler makes a tour of inspection."

sentences.zh: 彼無腹心之臣，五載一出，捐千里之畿，而誰與守邪？

translations.literal: Without heart-and-belly ministers, every five years he goes forth and abandons the thousand-li capital region — with whom is he to guard it?
translations.idiomatic: Without ministers of innermost counsel, the ruler goes abroad every five years and leaves the thousand-li capital region behind — who would guard it then?

sentences.zh: 今夫一家之中必有宗老，一介之士必有密友，以開心胸，以濟緩急，奈何天子而無腹心之臣乎？

translations.literal: Now in a single household there must be a clan elder; a single scholar must have a close friend — to open the breast and heart, to relieve urgency and delay — how can the Son of Heaven be without heart-and-belly ministers?
translations.idiomatic: Every household has its elder; every scholar has his confidant — to open the heart and meet urgent need. How then can the Son of Heaven lack ministers of innermost counsel?

sentences.zh: 近世之君抗然於上，而使宰相眇然於下，上下不接，而其志不通矣。

translations.literal: Rulers of recent times stand aloof above and make the chief minister dim and small below — above and below do not connect, and their intent does not pass through.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers of recent times hold themselves aloof above while keeping their chief ministers small below. Upper and lower no longer connect, and their minds no longer meet.

sentences.zh: 臣視君如天之遼然而不可親，而君亦如天之視人，泊然無愛之之心也。

translations.literal: Ministers regard the ruler as Heaven's vastness, not to be drawn near; the ruler likewise regards men as Heaven regards people — placid, without a heart of cherishing.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers see the ruler as remote as Heaven and beyond approach; the ruler sees his subjects as Heaven sees mankind — detached, without warmth.

sentences.zh: 是以社稷之憂，彼不以為憂，君憂不辱，君辱不死。

translations.literal: Thus the worry of altars and grain, they do not take as worry; the ruler's worry is not disgrace, the ruler's disgrace is not death.
translations.idiomatic: The peril of state and altar does not trouble them; their only concern is that the ruler not be disgraced, and that he not die in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 一人譽之則用之，一人毀之則捨之。

translations.literal: One man praises him and he is used; one man slanders him and he is cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: If one man praises an official, he is appointed; if one man slanders him, he is dismissed.

sentences.zh: 宰相避嫌畏譏且不暇，何暇盡心以憂社稷？

translations.literal: The chief minister, avoiding suspicion and fearing ridicule, has no leisure — what leisure to exhaust his heart in worrying over altars and grain?
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister, busy avoiding suspicion and ridicule, has no time left to devote himself to the welfare of the state.

sentences.zh: 數遷數易，視相府如傳捨。

translations.literal: Repeatedly transferred and repeatedly replaced, they regard the chief minister's residence as a relay inn.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred and replaced again and again, they treat the chief minister's office like a roadside inn.

sentences.zh: 百官泛泛於下，而天子惸惸於上，一旦有卒然之憂，吾未見其不顛沛而殞越也。

translations.literal: The hundred officials drift broadly below while the Son of Heaven stands solitary above — once there is sudden worry, I have not seen that they would not be overturned and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred officials drift below while the Son of Heaven stands alone above. When sudden crisis strikes, I do not see how the dynasty could avoid collapse.

sentences.zh: 聖人之任腹心之臣也，尊之如父師，愛之如兄弟，執手入臥內，同起居寢食，知無不言，言無不盡。

translations.literal: When the sage employs heart-and-belly ministers, he honors them as father and teacher, loves them as brothers, takes their hand and enters the inner chamber, shares rising, resting, sleeping, and eating — what is known is not unspoken, what is spoken is not incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: When the sage employs ministers of innermost counsel, he honors them as father and teacher, loves them as brothers, takes their hand into the inner chamber, and shares his daily life with them. Nothing known is left unsaid; nothing said is held back.

sentences.zh: 百人譽之不加密，百人毀之不加疏，尊其爵，厚其祿，重其權，而後可與議天下之機，慮天下之變。

translations.literal: A hundred men praise him without added closeness; a hundred men slander him without added distance — honor his rank, enrich his salary, weight his authority — only then can one deliberate with him on the stratagems of all under Heaven and consider the changes of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Let a hundred men praise him without drawing him closer, or slander him without pushing him away. Honor his rank, enrich his salary, and weight his authority — only then may one deliberate on the realm's stratagems and foresee its changes.

sentences.zh: 宰相韓琦見其書，善之，奏於朝，召試舍人院，辭疾不至，遂除秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Han Qi saw his book, approved it, presented it at court, summoned him for examination at the Academy of Scholarly Worthies — he declined on grounds of illness and did not come — and was therefore appointed Collator of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Han Qi read his work, admired it, and presented it at court. He was summoned for examination at the Academy of Scholarly Worthies but declined on grounds of illness and was instead appointed Collator of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會太常修纂建隆以來禮書，乃以為霸州文安縣主簿，與陳州項城令姚辟同修禮書，為《太常因革禮》一百卷。

translations.literal: When the Court of Imperial Sacrifices compiled ritual books from Jianlong onward, he was made Registrar of Wen'an County in Bazhou, and with Yao Pi, magistrate of Xiangcheng in Chenzhou, jointly compiled ritual books, producing the Court of Imperial Sacrifices: Rites of Reform in one hundred juan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Court of Imperial Sacrifices set about compiling ritual texts from the Jianlong reign onward, he was appointed Registrar of Wen'an County in Bazhou. Working with Yao Pi, magistrate of Xiangcheng in Chenzhou, he helped compile the Court of Imperial Sacrifices: Rites of Reform in one hundred juan.

sentences.zh: 書成，方奏未報，卒。

translations.literal: When the book was completed, it was just being presented and had not yet received response — he died.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished it had just been submitted to the throne but no response had yet come when he died.

sentences.zh: 賜其家縑、銀二百，子軾辭所賜，求贈官，特贈光祿寺丞，敕有司具舟載其喪歸蜀。

translations.literal: His family was granted two hundred bolts of silk and silver; his son Shi declined what was granted and requested a posthumous office — he was specially granted Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and the authorities were ordered to provide a boat to carry his coffin back to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted his family two hundred bolts of silk and silver. His son Shi declined the gifts and asked for a posthumous office for his father, who was specially granted Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. The authorities were ordered to provide a boat to carry his coffin back to Shu.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷、《謚法》三卷。

translations.literal: He had a collection of writings in twenty juan and Methods of Posthumous Titles in three juan.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included a collection of writings in twenty juan and Methods of Posthumous Titles in three juan.

sentences.zh: 章望之，字表民，建州浦城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Wangzhi, styled Biaomin, was a man of Pucheng in Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wangzhi, courtesy name Biaomin, was from Pucheng in Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 少孤，喜問學，志氣宏放。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he delighted in inquiry and study, with lofty spirit and expansive ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he loved learning and possessed a bold and expansive spirit.

sentences.zh: 為文辯博，長於議論。

translations.literal: In writing he was eloquent and broad, excelling in discourse and debate.
translations.idiomatic: His writing was eloquent and learned, and he excelled at argument.

sentences.zh: 初由伯父得像蔭為秘書省校書郎，監杭州茶庫。

translations.literal: At first through his uncle De Xiang's hereditary privilege he became Collator of the Secretariat and supervised the tea warehouse of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered office through his uncle Zhang De Xiang's hereditary privilege as Collator of the Secretariat and supervisor of the Hangzhou tea warehouse.

sentences.zh: 逾年辭疾去，求舉賢有方正，得像在相位，以嫌扼之，乃上書論時政凡萬餘言，不報。

translations.literal: After a year he resigned on grounds of illness, sought nomination for Worthy with Upright Conduct, but De Xiang was in the chief minister's seat and blocked him on grounds of kinship — he then submitted a memorial on current affairs of more than ten thousand words, with no response.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he resigned on grounds of illness and sought nomination as Worthy with Upright Conduct. Because De Xiang was chief minister and blocked him on grounds of kinship, he submitted a memorial of more than ten thousand words on current affairs, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，毀瘠過制。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he mourned until emaciated beyond the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he mourned until he was emaciated beyond what the regulations allowed.

sentences.zh: 服除，浮游江、淮間，犯艱苦，汲汲以營衣食，不自悔，人勸之仕，不應也。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he drifted between the Yangzi and Huai, braving hardship, urgently striving to secure food and clothing without regret; when people urged him to take office, he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he wandered between the Yangzi and Huai, enduring hardship and scrambling to earn a living without regret. When others urged him to take office, he refused.

sentences.zh: 其兄拱之知晉江縣，忤其守蔡襄，襄怒，誣以贓，貶。

translations.literal: His elder brother Gongzhi administered Jinjiang County, offended his prefect Cai Xiang — Xiang was angry, falsely accused him of corruption, and had him demoted.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Gongzhi served as magistrate of Jinjiang County and offended his superior Cai Xiang, who in anger falsely accused him of corruption and had him demoted.

sentences.zh: 望之號泣，力訴於朝。

translations.literal: Wangzhi wailed and wept, strenuously appealing to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi wept and appealed strenuously to the court.

sentences.zh: 時襄方貴顯，事久不得直。

translations.literal: At the time Xiang was just then noble and prominent; the matter long went without justice.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Cai Xiang was powerful and influential, and for a long time justice was not done.

sentences.zh: 望之訴不已，章十餘上，起獄數年，朝廷為再劾，卒脫拱之冤，復官如初，望之遂不復仕。

translations.literal: Wangzhi appealed without cease, submitting more than ten memorials, raising a case for several years; the court conducted a second investigation, and in the end cleared Gongzhi's injustice and restored his office as before — Wangzhi then never again took office.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi kept appealing, submitting more than ten memorials and setting a case in motion that lasted several years. The court conducted a second investigation, finally cleared Gongzhi's name, and restored his office. Wangzhi never took office again.

sentences.zh: 覃恩遷太常寺太祝、大理評事。

translations.literal: Through general grace he was promoted to Sacrificer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Through a general amnesty he was promoted to Sacrificer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士歐陽修、韓絳、知制誥吳奎劉敞、范鎮同薦其才，宰相欲稍用之，除簽書建康軍節度判官，不赴。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academicians Ouyang Xiu and Han Jiang, and Drafters of Edicts Wu Kui, Liu Chang, and Fan Zhen jointly recommended his talent; the chief minister wished to employ him somewhat — he was appointed Signing Judicial Administrator of the Jiankang Military Commission but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academicians Ouyang Xiu and Han Jiang, together with Drafters of Edicts Wu Kui, Liu Chang, and Fan Zhen, jointly recommended his talent. The chief minister wished to employ him and appointed him Signing Judicial Administrator of the Jiankang Military Commission, but he did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 又除知烏程縣，趣令受命，固辭，遂以光祿寺丞致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He was again appointed to administer Wucheng County, urged to accept the commission, firmly declined, and then retired as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed magistrate of Wucheng County and urged to accept, but firmly declined. He then retired as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and died.

sentences.zh: 望之喜議論，宗孟軻言性善，排荀卿、揚雄、韓愈、李翱之說，著《救性》七篇。

translations.literal: Wangzhi delighted in discourse, honored Mencius's saying that nature is good, rejected the teachings of Xunzi, Yang Xiong, Han Yu, and Li Ao, and wrote Saving Nature in seven chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi loved debate, upheld Mencius's doctrine that human nature is good, rejected the views of Xunzi, Yang Xiong, Han Yu, and Li Ao, and wrote Saving Nature in seven chapters.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修論魏、梁為正統，望之以為非，著《明統》三篇。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu argued that Wei and Liang were the legitimate succession; Wangzhi considered this wrong and wrote Clarifying Succession in three chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu argued that Wei and Liang held legitimate succession. Wangzhi disagreed and wrote Clarifying Succession in three chapters.

sentences.zh: 江南人李覯著《禮論》，謂仁、義、智、信、樂、刑、政皆出於禮，望之訂其說，著《禮論》一篇。

translations.literal: Li Gou of Jiangnan wrote Discourse on Rites, saying benevolence, righteousness, wisdom, faithfulness, music, punishment, and government all proceed from rites; Wangzhi revised his doctrine and wrote one chapter of Discourse on Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gou of Jiangnan wrote a Discourse on Rites arguing that benevolence, righteousness, wisdom, faithfulness, music, punishment, and government all spring from ritual. Wangzhi revised his argument in a single chapter of his own Discourse on Rites.

sentences.zh: 其議論多有過人者。

translations.literal: His discourses often surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his arguments surpassed those of his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 嘗北遊齊、趙，南泛湖、湘，西至汧、隴，東極吳會，山水勝處，無所不歷。

translations.literal: He once traveled north to Qi and Zhao, south across the lakes and Xiang, west to Qian and Long, east to the utmost Wu and Yue — scenic places of mountains and waters, none he did not visit.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled north to Qi and Zhao, south across the lakes and the Xiang region, west to Qian and Long, and east to Wu and Yue, visiting every celebrated landscape he could reach.

sentences.zh: 有歌詩、雜文數百篇，集為三十卷。

translations.literal: He had several hundred pieces of songs, poems, and miscellaneous writings, collected in thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left several hundred songs, poems, and essays, collected in thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 王逢，字會之，太平州當塗人。

translations.literal: Wang Feng, styled Huizhi, was a man of Dangtu in Taipingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Feng, courtesy name Huizhi, was from Dangtu in Taiping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其四世祖居巖，仕唐為驍衛長史，遭亂棄官，歸居青山。

translations.literal: His fourth-generation ancestor Ju Yan served Tang as Chief Clerk of the Valiant Guards, encountered turmoil and abandoned office, returning to dwell at Qingshan.
translations.idiomatic: His fourth-generation ancestor Wang Ju Yan had served the Tang as Chief Clerk of the Valiant Guards. When turmoil came he abandoned office and retired to Qingshan.

sentences.zh: 楊行密據淮南，使人以兵迫起之。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi held Huainan and sent men with troops to force him to rise.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xingmi seized Huainan, he sent troops to force Ju Yan back into service.

sentences.zh: 居巖散遣其家人，而以一身歸行密，授以湖州別駕，不遣。

translations.literal: Ju Yan dispersed and sent off his family, yet with his person alone returned to Xingmi — he was granted Vice Prefect of Huzhou but was not sent off.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Yan sent his family away and returned to Yang Xingmi alone. He was granted the post of Vice Prefect of Huzhou but was not allowed to leave.

sentences.zh: 一日，行密大會，失居巖，亟使人掩其家，無一人在者。

translations.literal: One day at a great gathering Xingmi lost Ju Yan, urgently sent men to surround his house — not a single person was there.
translations.idiomatic: One day at a great gathering Yang Xingmi found Ju Yan missing and hurriedly sent men to search his house, but not a soul was there.

sentences.zh: 其後有人於嵩山見空石室，詢其旁，或云有道人王居巖居此，去而莫知其所終。

translations.literal: Afterward someone at Mount Song saw an empty stone chamber; inquiring nearby, some said the Daoist Wang Ju Yan had dwelt here — he departed and none knew where he ended.
translations.idiomatic: Later someone at Mount Song saw an empty stone chamber. When he asked nearby, some said the Daoist Wang Ju Yan had lived there, but he had gone and no one knew where he ended his days.

sentences.zh: 子孫仕無顯者，至逢，博學能屬文，尤長於講說。

translations.literal: Descendants in office had none illustrious; reaching Feng, he was broadly learned and able to compose writing, especially excelling in lecturing and exposition.
translations.idiomatic: None of his descendants rose to prominence until Feng, who was broadly learned, skilled at composition, and especially gifted at lecturing.

sentences.zh: 少舉進士不中，去，教授蘇州，學者嘗數百人。

translations.literal: In youth he presented himself for the jinshi and did not pass, left, and taught in Suzhou — students at times numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He failed the jinshi examination in his youth, withdrew, and taught in Suzhou, where his students sometimes numbered several hundred.

sentences.zh: 晚始登第，補南雄州軍事判官，歸為國子監直講兼隴西郡王宅教授，李瑋從學，事之甚謹。

translations.literal: Only in his later years did he pass the examination, was appointed Military Judicial Administrator of Nanxiongzhou, returned to be Direct Lecturer of the Directorate of Education and concurrently instructor at the Prince of Longxi's residence — Li Wei followed his study and served him with great respect.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examination only late in life and was appointed Military Judicial Administrator of Nanxiong Prefecture. He then returned to serve as Direct Lecturer of the Directorate of Education and instructor at the residence of the Prince of Longxi. Li Wei studied under him and treated him with great respect.

sentences.zh: 岐國公主既降，瑋為逢求遷官，且有命，逢辭不受。

translations.literal: After the Princess of Qiguo had been given in marriage, Wei sought a transfer of office for Feng, and there was even an order — Feng declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: After the Princess of Qiguo was married, Wei sought a promotion for Feng and an order was even issued, but Feng declined to accept it.

sentences.zh: 久之，以太常博士通判徐州，卒。

translations.literal: After a long time, as Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices he served as deputy prefect of Xuzhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he served as Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and deputy prefect of Xuzhou, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 逢為人樂易，篤於朋友，與胡瑗最善。

translations.literal: Feng as a man was cheerful and easy, devoted to friends, and closest with Hu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was cheerful and easygoing, devoted to his friends, and closest to Hu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 喜著書，有《易傳》十卷、《乾德指說》一卷、《復書》七卷。

translations.literal: He delighted in writing books, having Commentary on the Changes in ten juan, Explanatory Points of Qiande in one juan, and Letters in Reply in seven juan.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to write and left a Commentary on the Changes in ten juan, Explanatory Points of Qiande in one juan, and Letters in Reply in seven juan.

sentences.zh: 妻陳氏亦有賢行，無子。

translations.literal: His wife, née Chen, also had worthy conduct; they had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, née Chen, was also a woman of virtue. They had no sons.

sentences.zh: 孫唐卿，字希元，青州人。

translations.literal: Sun Tangqing, styled Xiyuan, was a man of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tangqing, courtesy name Xiyuan, was from Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少有學行，年十七，以書謁韓琦，琦甚器之。

translations.literal: In youth he had learning and conduct; at age seventeen he presented a letter visiting Han Qi, and Qi greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: He showed learning and integrity from youth. At seventeen he presented a letter to Han Qi, who thought highly of him.

sentences.zh: 與黃庠、楊寘自景祐以來俱以進士為舉首，有名一時。

translations.literal: He, Huang Xiang, and Yang Zhi from the Jingyou period onward were all jinshi examination leaders, famous for a time.
translations.idiomatic: He, Huang Xiang, and Yang Zhi had all headed the jinshi lists since the Jingyou period and were celebrated in their day.

sentences.zh: 唐卿初中第，通判陝州，於吏事若素習。

translations.literal: When Tangqing first passed the examination and served as deputy prefect of Shanzhou, in official matters he seemed long practiced.
translations.idiomatic: When Tangqing first passed the examination and served as deputy prefect of Shanzhou, he handled official business as if he had long been practiced in it.

sentences.zh: 民有母再適人而死，及葬其父，恨母之不得祔，乃盜母之喪而同葬之。

translations.literal: A commoner had a mother who remarried and died; when burying his father, he resented that the mother could not be enshrined alongside — he stole the mother's coffin and buried it together.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner whose mother had remarried and died later buried his father. Angry that his mother could not be enshrined beside his father, he stole her coffin and buried her with him.

sentences.zh: 有司論以法，唐卿時權府事，乃曰：「是知有孝而不知有法爾。」

translations.literal: The authorities judged by law; Tangqing was then acting in prefectural affairs and said: "This one knows filial piety but does not know there is law."
translations.idiomatic: The authorities prosecuted the case according to law. Tangqing was then acting in prefectural affairs and said, "This man knows filial duty but does not know there is law."

sentences.zh: 乃釋之以聞。

translations.literal: He then released him and reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: He then released the man and reported the matter upward.

sentences.zh: 未幾，丁父憂，毀瘠嘔血而卒。

translations.literal: Before long, upon his father's death he mourned until emaciated, vomited blood, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, when his father died, he mourned until he was emaciated, vomited blood, and died.

sentences.zh: 詔賻其家。

translations.literal: An edict granted funeral gifts to his family.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered funeral gifts for his family.

sentences.zh: 黃庠字長善，洪州分寧人。

translations.literal: Huang Xiang, styled Changshan, was a man of Fenning in Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Xiang, courtesy name Changshan, was from Fenning in Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 博學強記，超敏過人。

translations.literal: Broadly learned with strong memory, surpassing keenness beyond other men.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly learned, possessed a formidable memory, and was extraordinarily quick-witted.

sentences.zh: 初至京師，就舉國子監、開封府、禮部，皆為第一。

translations.literal: When he first reached the capital and presented himself at the Directorate of Education, Kaifeng Prefecture, and the Ministry of Rites, he was first in all.
translations.idiomatic: When he first came to the capital and took the examinations at the Directorate of Education, Kaifeng Prefecture, and the Ministry of Rites, he ranked first in every one.

sentences.zh: 比引試崇政殿，以疾不得入，天子遣內侍即邸捨撫問，賜以藥劑。

translations.literal: When it came to the presentation examination at the Chongzheng Hall, on account of illness he could not enter; the Son of Heaven sent a palace attendant directly to his lodging to comfort and inquire, granting medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace examination at the Chongzheng Hall was held, illness kept him from attending. The emperor sent a palace attendant to his lodging to inquire after him and granted him medicine.

sentences.zh: 是時庠名聲動京師，所作程文，傳誦天下，聞於外夷，近世布衣罕比也。

translations.literal: At this time Xiang's fame shook the capital; the examination essays he composed were transmitted and recited throughout the realm, heard among outer barbarians — among commoners of recent times, few could be compared.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiang's fame shook the capital. His examination essays were read throughout the realm and even reached foreign lands — among commoners of recent times, few could compare with him.

sentences.zh: 歸江南五年，以病卒。

translations.literal: He returned to Jiangnan for five years and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Jiangnan for five years and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 楊寘字審賢，察之弟。

translations.literal: Yang Zhi, styled Shenxian, was the younger brother of Yang Cha.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhi, courtesy name Shenxian, was the younger brother of Yang Cha.

sentences.zh: 少有雋才，慶歷二年舉進士京師，試國子監、禮部皆第一。

translations.literal: In youth he had outstanding talent; in the second year of Qingli he presented himself for the jinshi in the capital — examinations at the Directorate of Education and Ministry of Rites were both first.
translations.idiomatic: He showed outstanding talent from youth. In the second year of Qingli he took the jinshi examination in the capital and ranked first in both the Directorate of Education and Ministry of Rites examinations.

sentences.zh: 既試崇政殿，帝臨軒啟封，見名，喜動於色，謂輔臣曰：「楊寘也。」

translations.literal: After the examination at the Chongzheng Hall, the emperor personally at the hall opened the seal, saw the name, and delight moved his countenance; he said to assisting ministers: "It is Yang Zhi."
translations.idiomatic: At the Chongzheng Hall examination the emperor personally opened the sealed list, saw the name, and delight showed on his face. He said to his ministers, "It is Yang Zhi."

sentences.zh: 遂擢第一，公卿相賀為得人。

translations.literal: He was then elevated to first place; dukes and ministers congratulated one another that a worthy man had been obtained.
translations.idiomatic: He was placed first, and the high officials congratulated one another that the court had found a true talent.

sentences.zh: 授將作監丞、通判穎州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Construction and deputy prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Construction and deputy prefect of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未至官，持母喪，病羸卒，特詔賻恤其家。

translations.literal: Before reaching his post he was in mourning for his mother, died emaciated from illness, and a special edict granted funeral gifts and relief to his family.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up his post he entered mourning for his mother, then died wasted by illness. A special edict granted funeral gifts and relief to his family.

sentences.zh: 先是，其友夢寘作龍首山人，寘自謂：「龍首，我四冠多士；

translations.literal: Earlier, his friend dreamed that Zhi became the Mountain Man of Dragon Head; Zhi himself said: "Dragon Head — I four times topped the many scholars;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a friend dreamed that Zhi had become the Mountain Man of Dragon Head. Zhi himself said, "Dragon Head — I four times topped the scholars;

sentences.zh: 山人，無祿位之稱。

translations.literal: "mountain man" is a title without salary and office.
translations.idiomatic: mountain man is a title without rank or salary.

sentences.zh: 我其終是乎！」

translations.literal: Will my end be this!"
translations.idiomatic: Is that how my life will end?"

sentences.zh: 已而果然。

translations.literal: Before long it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: Before long it proved true.

sentences.zh: 唐庚，字子西，眉州丹稜人也。

translations.literal: Tang Geng, styled Zixi, was a man of Danleng in Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Geng, courtesy name Zixi, was from Danleng in Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 善屬文，舉進士，稍為宗子博士，張商英薦其才，除提舉京畿常平。

translations.literal: Skilled at composing writing, he passed the jinshi, was gradually made Doctor for the Imperial Clan, Zhang Shangying recommended his talent, and he was appointed Commissioner for the Metropolitan Ever-Normal Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at composition, he passed the jinshi examination and was gradually appointed Doctor for the Imperial Clan. Zhang Shangying recommended his talent, and he was appointed Commissioner for the Metropolitan Ever-Normal Granaries.

sentences.zh: 商英罷相，庚亦坐貶，安置惠州。

translations.literal: When Shangying was removed as chief minister, Geng also sat in demotion and was settled at Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shangying was dismissed as chief minister, Geng was also demoted and exiled to Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 會赦，復官承議郎，提舉上清太平宮。

translations.literal: At an amnesty he was restored to office as Gentleman for Discussion, Commissioner for the Upper Clarity and Great Peace Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At an amnesty he was restored to office as Gentleman for Discussion and appointed Commissioner for the Upper Clarity and Great Peace Palace.

sentences.zh: 歸蜀，道病卒。

translations.literal: Returning to Shu, he died of illness on the road.
translations.idiomatic: On his way back to Shu he fell ill on the road and died.

sentences.zh: 年五十一。

translations.literal: Age fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-one years old.

sentences.zh: 庚為文精密，通於世務，作《名治》、《察言》、《閔俗》、《存舊》、《內前行》諸篇，時人稱之。

translations.literal: Geng's writing was precise and close, penetrating worldly affairs; he wrote such pieces as Naming Good Government, Examining Words, Pitying Custom, Preserving the Old, and Within the Palace Advance — men of the time praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Geng wrote with precision and understood practical affairs. He composed such works as Naming Good Government, Examining Words, Pitying Custom, Preserving the Old, and Within the Palace Advance, which his contemporaries praised.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collection of writings in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collection of writings in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 子文若，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Wenruo has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenruo has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 庚兄弟五人，長兄瞻，字望之，後改名伯虎，字長孺。

translations.literal: Geng had five brothers; the eldest brother Zhan, styled Wangzhi, later changed his name to Bohu, styled Changru.
translations.idiomatic: Geng had five brothers. The eldest, Zhan, courtesy name Wangzhi, later changed his name to Bohu and took the courtesy name Changru.

sentences.zh: 治《易》、《春秋》，皆有家法。

translations.literal: He studied the Changes and Spring and Autumn Annals, both with family methods.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals, each according to his family's scholarly tradition.

sentences.zh: 元祐三年，其父游瀘南，伯虎兄弟居母喪於丹山，伯虎夜半蹴庚曰：「吾夢收父書，發之，得『亟來』二字，吾父得無他乎？

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanyou, their father was traveling in southern Lu; the Bohu brothers were in mourning for their mother at Danshan — at midnight Bohu kicked Geng and said: "I dreamed receiving father's letter; opening it, I obtained the two words 'come quickly' — could father be in some other trouble?
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanyou their father was traveling in southern Lu while Bohu and his brothers were mourning their mother at Danshan. At midnight Bohu kicked Geng awake and said, "I dreamed I received a letter from Father. When I opened it I found only two words: 'Come quickly.' Could something be wrong with him?

sentences.zh: 吾心動矣。

translations.literal: My heart is moved.
translations.idiomatic: My heart is troubled.

sentences.zh: 汝奉母奠朝夕，吾趨瀘南。」

translations.literal: You attend mother's offerings morning and evening; I hurry to southern Lu."
translations.idiomatic: You tend Mother's grave morning and evening. I will hurry to southern Lu."

sentences.zh: 庚未及應，伯虎奮曰：「吾決矣！」

translations.literal: Before Geng could respond, Bohu roused himself and said: "I have decided!"
translations.idiomatic: Before Geng could answer, Bohu cried out, "My mind is made up!"

sentences.zh: 起裹糧，黎明走洪川僦舟，遇江漲，聲搖數十里，客舟皆艤岸不敢動，伯虎彷徨堤上，有漁者持小艇系港中，啖以厚利，不許。

translations.literal: He rose, wrapped provisions, at dawn ran to Hongchuan to hire a boat — encountering the river in flood, the sound shook for several tens of li, passenger boats all moored at shore and dared not move; Bohu paced the embankment — a fisherman held a small skiff moored in the harbor, offered thick profit, but he would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: He packed food at once and at dawn ran to Hongchuan to hire a boat. The river was in flood and its roar shook the shore for miles. Passenger boats all lay at anchor and dared not move. Bohu paced the embankment until he found a fisherman with a small skiff moored in the harbor. He offered a large reward, but the man refused.

sentences.zh: 伯虎超入艇中，叱僕夫解維，漁者不得已，從之。

translations.literal: Bohu leaped into the skiff, shouted at the servant to cast off the mooring — the fisherman had no choice and followed.
translations.idiomatic: Bohu leaped into the skiff and ordered his servant to cast off. The fisherman had no choice but to go with him.

sentences.zh: 二日半至瀘南，父果病甚，見伯虎，大驚，問其故，具告之。

translations.literal: In two and a half days he reached southern Lu; father was indeed gravely ill — seeing Bohu, he was greatly startled, asked the reason, and was told in full.
translations.idiomatic: In two and a half days he reached southern Lu. His father was indeed gravely ill. Seeing Bohu, he was greatly startled and asked the reason. Bohu told him everything.

sentences.zh: 父歎曰：「天告汝也！」

translations.literal: Father sighed and said: "Heaven informed you!"
translations.idiomatic: His father sighed and said, "Heaven told you!"

sentences.zh: 是日，疾少間，伯虎具舟侍父以歸。

translations.literal: That day the illness eased somewhat; Bohu prepared a boat and attended father home.
translations.idiomatic: That day his illness eased somewhat. Bohu prepared a boat and escorted his father home.

sentences.zh: 居數日，疾復作，遂卒。

translations.literal: After several days the illness returned and he died.
translations.idiomatic: After several days the illness returned, and he died.

sentences.zh: 元符二年，庚以貢舉事系獄臨邛，語連伯虎，臨邛並械之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfu, Geng was imprisoned at Linqiong on a matter of the civil service examinations; his testimony implicated Bohu, and Linqiong shackled them both.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanfu, Tang Geng was imprisoned at Linqiong on charges related to the civil service examinations. His testimony implicated Shi Bohu, and the authorities shackled them both.

sentences.zh: 凡對吏逾年，掠治無完膚，其詞確然，一不及庚，以故獄久不具，卒會赦，除之。

translations.literal: In all, facing the officials for more than a year, under torture his body had no intact skin; his words were clearly established, yet not one word implicated Geng — for this reason the case long remained incomplete, until by chance an amnesty came and it was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Interrogated for more than a year, he was tortured until not a patch of skin was left whole. His testimony was clear and firm, yet not a single word implicated Geng. The case therefore dragged on without conclusion until, by chance, an amnesty was declared and the charges were dropped.

sentences.zh: 伯虎性真率，無威儀，人多易之，至是皆大服，以為不可及。

translations.literal: Bohu's nature was honest and forthright, without imposing dignity; many people treated him lightly — now they were all greatly convinced, thinking him beyond reach.
translations.idiomatic: Bohu was honest and unpretentious, with none of the bearing that commands respect, and many people had taken him lightly. Now they were all deeply impressed and regarded him as beyond comparison.

sentences.zh: 伯虎仕於四方，每數年一歸，不過旬日復去。

translations.literal: Bohu served in various places; every few years he returned once, staying no more than ten days before leaving again.
translations.idiomatic: Bohu held office in various regions. Every few years he would return home once, stay no more than ten days, and then leave again.

sentences.zh: 後卒於家，有子二人。

translations.literal: Later he died at home; he had two sons.
translations.idiomatic: He later died at home. He left two sons.

sentences.zh: 文同，字與可，梓州梓潼人，漢文翁之後，蜀人猶以「石室」名其家。

translations.literal: Wen Tong, styled Yu Ke, was a man of Zitong in Zizhou, a descendant of Wen Weng of Han; people of Shu still called his family the "Stone Chamber."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tong, styled Yu Ke, was a native of Zitong in Zizhou and a descendant of Wen Weng of Han. People in Shu still called his family the "Stone Chamber."

sentences.zh: 同方口秀眉，以學名世，操韻高潔，自號笑笑先生。

translations.literal: Tong had a square mouth and fine brows; he was famed throughout the age for learning, his temperament lofty and pure, and styled himself Master Smiling Smiling.
translations.idiomatic: Tong had a square mouth and fine brows. He was renowned in his time for scholarship, his character lofty and refined, and he styled himself Master Smiling Smiling.

sentences.zh: 善詩、文、篆、隸、行、草、飛白。

translations.literal: He excelled at poetry, prose, seal script, clerical script, running script, cursive script, and flying-white calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at poetry, prose, seal script, clerical script, running script, cursive script, and flying-white calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 文彥博守成都，奇之，致書同曰：「與可襟韻灑落，如晴雲秋月，塵埃不到。」

translations.literal: When Wen Yanbo served as prefect of Chengdu, he marveled at him and wrote to Tong: "Yu Ke's bearing and spirit are free and lofty, like bright clouds in clear weather or the autumn moon — dust never touches him."
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Yanbo was prefect of Chengdu, he was struck by Tong's talent and wrote to him: "Yu Ke's bearing and spirit are free and unburdened, like bright clouds on a clear day or the autumn moon — no dust ever settles on them."

sentences.zh: 司馬光、蘇軾尤敬重之。

translations.literal: Sima Guang and Su Shi especially honored and esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang and Su Shi held him in especially high regard.

sentences.zh: 軾，同之從表弟也。

translations.literal: Shi was Tong's younger cousin on the mother's side.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi was Tong's younger cousin on the mother's side.

sentences.zh: 同又善畫竹，初不自貴重，四方之人持縑素請者，足相躡於門。

translations.literal: Tong was also skilled at painting bamboo; at first he did not prize his own work, yet people from all quarters came with silk requesting paintings, their feet treading on one another at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was also skilled at painting bamboo. At first he did not think much of his own work, yet people from all directions came with silk scrolls to request paintings, their feet crowding one another at his gate.

sentences.zh: 同厭之，投縑於地，罵曰：「吾將以為襪。」

translations.literal: Tong grew weary of this; he threw the silk on the ground and cursed: "I'll use this for socks."
translations.idiomatic: Tong grew tired of it. He threw the silk on the ground and cursed, "I'll use this for socks."

sentences.zh: 好事者傳之以為口實。

translations.literal: Gossips spread the story as a standing joke.
translations.idiomatic: Lovers of gossip spread the story and made it a standing joke.

sentences.zh: 初舉進士，稍遷太常博士、集賢校理，知陵州，又知洋州。

translations.literal: He first passed the jinshi examination and was gradually promoted to Erudite of the Grand Secretariat of Rites, collating editor of the Hall for Veneration of Worthies, and prefect of Lingzhou, then prefect of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He first passed the jinshi examination and was gradually promoted to Erudite of the Grand Secretariat of Rites and collating editor of the Hall for Veneration of Worthies. He served as prefect of Lingzhou and later of Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，知湖州，明年，至陳州宛丘驛，忽留不行，沐浴衣冠，正坐而卒。
