translations.literal: At the start of Yuanfeng, he became prefect of Huzhou; the next year, when he reached Wanshou Post Station in Chenzhou, he suddenly stopped and would not go on. He bathed, dressed in proper attire, sat upright, and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanfeng era he was appointed prefect of Huzhou. The following year, when he reached Wanshou Post Station in Chen Prefecture, he suddenly stopped and would not go on. He bathed, put on proper dress, sat upright, and died.

sentences.zh: 崔公度嘗與同同為館職，見同京南，殊無言，及將別，但云：「明日復來乎？

translations.literal: Cui Gongdu had once held the same palace editorial post as Tong. He saw Tong south of the capital; Tong said almost nothing, and as they were about to part, only said: "Will you come again tomorrow?
translations.idiomatic: Cui Gongdu had once held the same palace editorial post as Tong. He saw Tong south of the capital. Tong said almost nothing, and as they were about to part he only asked, "Will you come again tomorrow?

sentences.zh: 與子話。」

translations.literal: To talk with you."
translations.idiomatic: To talk with you?"

sentences.zh: 公度意以「話」為「畫」，明日再往，同曰：「與公話。」

translations.literal: Gongdu took "talk" to mean "paint"; the next day he went again, and Tong said: "To talk with you."
translations.idiomatic: Gongdu took "talk" to mean "paint." The next day he went again, and Tong said, "To talk with you."

sentences.zh: 則左右顧，恐有聽者。

translations.literal: Then he looked left and right, fearing listeners.
translations.idiomatic: Then he looked left and right, afraid someone might be listening.

sentences.zh: 公度方知同將有言，非畫也。

translations.literal: Gongdu then understood that Tong intended to speak, not to paint.
translations.idiomatic: Gongdu then realized that Tong meant to speak with him, not to paint for him.

sentences.zh: 同曰：「吾聞人不妄語者，舌可過鼻。」

translations.literal: Tong said: "I have heard that one who does not speak rashly can touch his tongue to his nose."
translations.idiomatic: Tong said, "I have heard that a man who never speaks rashly can touch his tongue to his nose."

sentences.zh: 即吐其舌，三疊之如餅狀，引之至眉間，公度大驚。

translations.literal: Thereupon he thrust out his tongue, folded it three times like a cake, and drew it up to between his brows — Gongdu was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Then he thrust out his tongue, folded it three times like a flat cake, and drew it up to his brow. Gongdu was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 及京中傳同死，公度乃悟所見非生者。

translations.literal: When word spread in the capital that Tong had died, Gongdu then realized that what he had seen was not a living man.
translations.idiomatic: When word spread in the capital that Tong had died, Gongdu realized that what he had seen was not a living man.

sentences.zh: 有《丹淵集》四十卷行於世。

translations.literal: His Danyuan Collection in forty scrolls circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Danyuan Collection in forty scrolls circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 楊傑，字次公，無為人。

translations.literal: Yang Jie, styled Cigong, was a man of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jie, styled Cigong, was a native of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 少有名於時，舉進士。

translations.literal: He had early renown in his time and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He won early renown and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 元豐中，官太常者數任，一時禮樂之事，皆預討論。

translations.literal: During Yuanfeng he held several posts in the Grand Secretariat of Rites; he participated in discussion of all matters of ritual and music of the time.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfeng era he held several posts in the Grand Secretariat of Rites and took part in deliberations on all the ritual and music issues of the day.

sentences.zh: 嘗議玉牒帝系自僖祖而上，世次莫知，則僖祖為始祖無疑，宜以僖祖配感生帝。

translations.literal: He once argued that in the imperial genealogy recorded in the jade registers, from Emperor Xizu upward the generations were unknown — thus Xizu as founding ancestor was beyond doubt, and he should be paired with the Spirit-Engendering Emperor in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: He once argued that in the imperial genealogy recorded in the jade registers, the generations above Emperor Xizu were unknown, so there could be no doubt that Xizu was the founding ancestor and that he should be paired with the Spirit-Engendering Emperor in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 又請孝惠賀後、淑德尹後、章懷潘後皆祖宗首納之後，孝章宋後嘗母儀天下，升祔之禮，久而未講，宜因慈聖光獻崇配之日，升四後神主祔於祖宗祏室，斷天下之大疑，正宗廟之大法。

translations.literal: He also petitioned that Empress Xiaohui He, Empress Shude Yin, and Empress Zhanghuai Pan were all the first consorts taken into the imperial household by the founding ancestors, and Empress Xiaozhang Song had once held the motherly model for all under Heaven — yet the rite of elevating their spirit tablets for joint enshrinement had long gone undiscussed; on the day when Empress Dowager Cisheng Guangxian received exalted pairing in sacrifice, the spirit tablets of the four empresses should be elevated and enshrined in the ancestral shrine chamber, settling the great doubt of the empire and establishing the great law of the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned that Empress Xiaohui He, Empress Shude Yin, and Empress Zhanghuai Pan had all been the first consorts taken into the imperial household by the founding ancestors, and that Empress Xiaozhang Song had once held the motherly model for all under Heaven, yet the rite of elevating their spirit tablets for joint enshrinement had long gone undiscussed. On the day when Empress Dowager Cisheng Guangxian received exalted pairing in sacrifice, the spirit tablets of the four empresses should be elevated and enshrined in the ancestral shrine chamber, thereby settling a great doubt throughout the empire and establishing the fundamental law of the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 由是四後始得升祔。

translations.literal: From this the four empresses were at last able to be elevated for joint enshrinement.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, the four empresses were at last able to be elevated for joint enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 神宗詔秘書監劉幾、禮部侍郎范鎮議樂，幾請命傑同議。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong ordered Vice Director of the Secretariat Liu Ji and Vice Minister of Rites Fan Zhen to discuss music; Ji requested that Jie join the deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong ordered Vice Director of the Secretariat Liu Ji and Vice Minister of Rites Fan Zhen to deliberate on music, and Ji requested that Jie join the discussion.

sentences.zh: 傑言大樂七失，併圖上之。

translations.literal: Jie stated seven errors of the grand music and submitted them together with diagrams.
translations.idiomatic: Jie identified seven flaws in the grand music and submitted his findings together with diagrams.

sentences.zh: 神宗下幾、鎮參定，鎮不用傑議，自制。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Ji and Zhen to examine and fix it; Zhen did not use Jie's proposals and made his own system.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Ji and Zhen to examine and revise the system. Zhen did not adopt Jie's proposals and devised his own.

sentences.zh: 樂成，詔褒之。

translations.literal: When the music was completed, an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When the music was completed, an edict praised Fan Zhen.

sentences.zh: 元豐末，晉州教授陸長愈言：「近封孟軻鄒國公，宜春秋釋奠，與顏子並配。」

translations.literal: Late in Yuanfeng, Instructor Lu Changyu of Jin Prefecture said: "Meng Ke was recently enfeoffed as Duke of Zou — in the spring and autumn sacrificial rites to Confucius, he should be paired equally with Yan Hui."
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Yuanfeng era, Instructor Lu Changyu of Jin Prefecture said, "Meng Ke was recently enfeoffed as Duke of Zou. In the spring and autumn sacrificial rites to Confucius, he should be paired equally with Yan Hui."

sentences.zh: 下太常議，傑與少卿葉均、博士盛陶、王古、辛公佐以謂凡配享從祀，皆孔子同時之人，今以孟軻並配非是。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the Grand Secretariat of Rites for deliberation; Jie, Vice Director Ye Jun, and Erudites Sheng Tao, Wang Gu, and Xin Gongzuo held that all who received paired sacrifice or secondary enshrinement were contemporaries of Confucius — to pair Meng Ke equally now was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the Grand Secretariat of Rites for deliberation. Jie, Vice Director Ye Jun, and Erudites Sheng Tao, Wang Gu, and Xin Gongzuo argued that all those who received paired sacrifice or secondary enshrinement had been contemporaries of Confucius, and that pairing Meng Ke equally with Yan Hui would be improper.

sentences.zh: 禮部復言：「自唐至今，以伏勝、高堂生等二十一賢從祀，豈必同時人？」

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites replied: "From Tang until now, twenty-one worthies including Fu Sheng and Master Gaotang have received secondary enshrinement — must they all be contemporaries?"
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites replied, "From the Tang dynasty to the present, twenty-one worthies including Fu Sheng and Master Gaotang have received secondary enshrinement. Were they all contemporaries of Confucius?"

sentences.zh: 詔從禮部議。

translations.literal: An edict followed the Ministry of Rites' proposal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed the Ministry of Rites' proposal.

sentences.zh: 哲宗即位，議樂，又用范鎮說。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, music was again discussed and Fan Zhen's views were used once more.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, music was discussed again and Fan Zhen's views were adopted once more.

sentences.zh: 傑復破鎮樂章曲名、宮架加磬、十六鐘磬之非。

translations.literal: Jie again refuted Zhen's errors regarding names of music sections, adding chime stones to the palace frame, and the sixteen bells and chime stones.
translations.idiomatic: Jie again refuted Zhen's errors regarding the names of music sections, the addition of chime stones to the palace frame, and the use of sixteen bells and chime stones.

sentences.zh: 又論鎮以黑黍用秠制律、銅量，叩之不合黃鐘，以世無真黍，用太府尺為樂尺，下舊樂三律。

translations.literal: He further argued that Zhen used black millet of the finest grade to establish pitch pipes and a copper measure, yet when struck they did not match the Yellow Bell; because there was no genuine millet in the age, he used the Grand Treasury foot-ruler as the music ruler, lowering the old music by three pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: He further argued that Zhen had used black millet of the finest grade to establish pitch pipes and a copper measure, yet when struck they did not match the Yellow Bell. Because genuine millet could not be found in the age, Zhen used the Grand Treasury foot-ruler as the music ruler and lowered the old music by three pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 詳具《樂志》。

translations.literal: Details are fully set forth in the Treatise on Music.
translations.idiomatic: The details are fully set forth in the Treatise on Music.

sentences.zh: 傑在神宗時與鎮異議，至是復攻之，鎮之樂律卒不用。

translations.literal: Jie had differed from Zhen during Shenzong's reign; now he attacked him again, and Zhen's pitch system was ultimately not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Jie had differed from Zhen during Shenzong's reign, and now he attacked him again. Zhen's pitch system was ultimately not adopted.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，為禮部員外郎，出知潤州，除兩浙提點刑獄，卒，年七十。

translations.literal: During Yuanyou he was Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites, then went out to serve as prefect of Runzhou, was appointed judicial intendant of the Two Zhe circuits, and died at age seventy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanyou era he served as Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites, then went out as prefect of Runzhou and was appointed judicial intendant of the Two Zhe circuits. He died at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 自號無為子，有文集二十餘卷，《樂記》五卷。

translations.literal: He styled himself Master of Nonaction; he had a collected writings of more than twenty scrolls and a Record of Music in five scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself Master of Nonaction. He left a collected writings of more than twenty scrolls and a Record of Music in five scrolls.

sentences.zh: 賀鑄，字方回，衛州人，孝惠皇后之族孫。

translations.literal: He Zhu, styled Fanghui, was a man of Weizhou, a descendant of Empress Xiaohui on the maternal line.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhu, styled Fanghui, was a native of Weizhou and a descendant of Empress Xiaohui on the maternal line.

sentences.zh: 長七尺，面鐵色，眉目聳拔。

translations.literal: He stood seven feet, his face iron-colored, his brows and eyes lofty and striking.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven feet tall, with an iron-dark face and lofty, striking brows and eyes.

sentences.zh: 喜談當世事，可否不少假借，雖貴要權傾一時，小不中意，極口詆之無遺辭，人以為近俠。

translations.literal: He loved to discuss affairs of the day, right or wrong, without the least concession; even when a noble or powerful man who dominated the age displeased him in the slightest, he would denounce him to the full without leaving a word — people considered him nearly a knight-errant.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to discuss current affairs and would concede nothing on right or wrong. Even when a powerful noble who dominated the age displeased him in the slightest, he would denounce him without restraint. People regarded him as nearly a knight-errant.

sentences.zh: 博學強記，工語言，深婉麗密，如次組繡。

translations.literal: Broad in learning and strong in memory, he was skilled with language — deep, graceful, dense, and fine, like layered embroidery.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly learned and had a powerful memory, and he was skilled with language — deep, graceful, dense, and fine, like layered embroidery.

sentences.zh: 尤長於度曲，掇拾人所棄遺，少加隱括，皆為新奇。

translations.literal: He was especially adept at composing tunes; gathering what others had cast aside or abandoned, with slight reshaping all became novel creations.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially adept at composing tunes. He would gather what others had cast aside, reshape it slightly, and turn it into something wholly new.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「吾筆端驅使李商隱、溫庭筠常奔命不暇。」

translations.literal: He once said: "At my writing brush I drive Li Shangyin and Wen Tingyun as though they were constantly racing on urgent orders without a moment to spare."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "At my brush I drive Li Shangyin and Wen Tingyun as though they were constantly racing on urgent orders without a moment to spare."

sentences.zh: 諸公貴人多客致之，鑄或從或不從，其所不欲見，終不貶也。

translations.literal: Many lords and nobles sent clients to invite him; Zhu sometimes accepted and sometimes did not — those he did not wish to see, he never humbled himself to visit.
translations.idiomatic: Many lords and nobles sent clients to invite him. Zhu sometimes accepted and sometimes refused. As for those he did not wish to see, he never humbled himself to visit them.

sentences.zh: 初，娶宗女，隸籍右選，監太原工作，有貴人子同事，驕倨不相下。

translations.literal: At first he married an imperial clanswoman and was listed in the right branch of selection; he supervised construction work at Taiyuan. A nobleman's son served alongside him, proud and haughty, neither yielding to the other.
translations.idiomatic: At first he married an imperial clanswoman and was listed in the right branch of the selection rolls. He supervised construction work at Taiyuan, where a nobleman's son served alongside him. Both were proud and haughty, and neither would yield to the other.

sentences.zh: 鑄廉得盜工作物，屏侍吏，閉之密室，以杖數曰：「來，若某時盜某物為某用，某時盜某物入於家，然乎？」

translations.literal: Zhu, through investigation, discovered the nobleman's son had stolen work materials. He dismissed the attendants, shut him in a private room, and with a stick counted off: "Come — didn't you at such-and-such time steal such-and-such thing for such-and-such use, and at such-and-such time steal such-and-such thing and bring it home — is it so?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu discovered through investigation that the nobleman's son had stolen work materials. He dismissed the attendants, shut him in a private room, and with a stick in hand counted off each offense: "Come — didn't you steal such-and-such thing at such-and-such time for such-and-such use, and steal such-and-such thing at such-and-such time and bring it home? Is it so?"

sentences.zh: 貴人子惶駭謝「有之」。

translations.literal: The nobleman's son, terrified, apologized: "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: The nobleman's son, terrified, apologized and admitted, "It is so."

sentences.zh: 鑄曰：「能從吾治，免白髮。」

translations.literal: Zhu said: "If you can submit to my punishment, I'll spare reporting you."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu said, "If you can submit to my punishment, I'll spare reporting you."

sentences.zh: 即起自袒其膚，杖之數下，貴人子叩頭祈哀，即大笑釋去。

translations.literal: Thereupon he rose, bared the youth's back, and struck him several blows with the stick; the nobleman's son kowtowed and begged for mercy, whereupon Zhu laughed heartily and let him go.
translations.idiomatic: Then he rose, bared the youth's back, and struck him several blows with the stick. The nobleman's son kowtowed and begged for mercy, and Zhu immediately laughed and let him go.

sentences.zh: 自是諸挾氣力頡頏者，皆側目不敢仰視。

translations.literal: From then on, all who relied on force and contended for superiority looked askance and did not dare look up at him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, all who relied on force and contended for superiority looked askance at him and did not dare meet his gaze.

sentences.zh: 是時，江、淮間有米芾以魁岸奇譎知名，鑄以氣俠雄爽適相先後，二人每相遇，瞋目抵掌，論辯鋒起，終日各不能屈，談者爭傳為口實。

translations.literal: At that time Mi Fu of the Jiang-Huai region was famed for his imposing stature and strange brilliance; Zhu, with his chivalrous boldness and heroic openness, matched him in succession. Whenever the two met, they would glare and slap palms, debates flaring sharp, all day neither could overcome the other — onlookers competed to spread the tales as standing anecdotes.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Mi Fu of the Jiang-Huai region was famed for his imposing stature and strange brilliance, while Zhu, with his chivalrous boldness and heroic openness, matched him in spirit. Whenever the two met, they would glare and slap their palms together, sharp debate flaring up, and all day neither could prevail over the other. Onlookers competed to spread the stories as standing anecdotes.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，李清臣執政，奏換通直郎、通判泗州，又倅太平州。

translations.literal: During Yuanyou, with Li Qingchen holding power, he memorialized for Zhu's transfer as Gentleman for Direct Remonstrance and auxiliary prefect of Sizhou, then deputy prefect of Taiping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanyou era, with Li Qingchen in power, he memorialized for Zhu's appointment as Gentleman for Direct Remonstrance and auxiliary prefect of Sizhou, and later as deputy prefect of Taiping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 竟以尚氣使酒，不得美官，悒悒不得志，食宮祠祿，退居吳下，稍務引遠世故，亦無復軒輊如平日。

translations.literal: In the end, because he was proud and given to drink, he never obtained a fine office; gloomy and unfulfilled, he lived on stipends from a sinecure post, retired to the Wu region, gradually seeking to keep worldly affairs at a distance — and no longer weighed things in judgment as in former days.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, because he was proud and given to drink, he never obtained a fine office. Gloomy and unfulfilled, he lived on stipends from a sinecure post and retired to the Wu region. He gradually sought to keep worldly affairs at a distance and no longer passed judgment as sharply as he had in former days.

sentences.zh: 家藏書萬餘卷，手自校讎，無一字誤，以是杜門將遂其老。

translations.literal: His household held more than ten thousand scrolls of books; he personally collated them with not a single erroneous character — thus he closed his doors to spend his old age.
translations.idiomatic: His household held more than ten thousand scrolls of books, which he personally collated without a single erroneous character. He closed his doors and intended to spend his old age in that way.

sentences.zh: 家貧，貸子錢自給，有負者，輒折券與之，秋毫不以丐人。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he lent money for interest to support himself. When someone owed him, he would tear up the contract and give it to them — never begging anyone for the slightest thing.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor, and he supported himself by lending money at interest. When someone owed him, he would tear up the contract and give it to them, never begging anyone for the slightest thing.

sentences.zh: 鑄所為詞章，往往傳播在人口。

translations.literal: Zhu's compositions often spread among people's lips.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu's compositions often spread by word of mouth.

sentences.zh: 建中靖國時，黃庭堅自黔中還，得其「江南梅子」之句，以為似謝玄暉。

translations.literal: During Jianzhong Jingguo, Huang Tingjian returned from Qianzhong and obtained his line about "plums of Jiangnan," thinking it resembled Xie Xuanyu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianzhong Jingguo era, Huang Tingjian returned from Qianzhong and came upon Zhu's line about "plums of Jiangnan," which he thought resembled the poetry of Xie Xuanyu.

sentences.zh: 其所與交，終始厚者，惟信安程俱。

translations.literal: Of those with whom he associated, the only one who remained close from beginning to end was Cheng Ju of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Of those with whom he associated, the only one who remained close from beginning to end was Cheng Ju of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 鑄自裒歌詞，名《東山樂府》，俱為序之。

translations.literal: Zhu himself compiled his song lyrics under the title Eastern Mountain Music Bureau; Ju wrote the preface.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu himself compiled his song lyrics under the title Eastern Mountain Music Bureau, and Cheng Ju wrote the preface.

sentences.zh: 嘗自言唐諫議大夫知章之後，且推本其初，出王子慶忌，以慶為姓，居越之湖澤所謂鏡湖者，本慶湖也，避漢安帝父清河王諱，改為賀氏，慶湖亦轉為鏡。

translations.literal: He once claimed himself a descendant of Tang Remonstrance-in-Chief He Zhizhang, and tracing the lineage back further derived from Prince Qingji of Wu; taking Qing as the surname, they dwelt at Mirror Lake in Yue — the so-called Celebratory Lake, later changed to the He clan to avoid the taboo name of the Han Emperor's father, the Prince of Qinghe — and Celebratory Lake in turn became Mirror Lake.
translations.idiomatic: He once claimed to be a descendant of Tang Remonstrance-in-Chief He Zhizhang, and tracing the lineage back further derived it from Prince Qingji of Wu. His ancestors had taken Qing as their surname and lived at Mirror Lake in Yue — originally called Celebratory Lake. To avoid the taboo name of the Han emperor's father, the Prince of Qinghe, the clan changed its name to He, and Celebratory Lake in turn became Mirror Lake.

sentences.zh: 當時不知何所據。

translations.literal: At the time no one knew on what basis he claimed this.
translations.idiomatic: At the time no one knew on what basis he made this claim.

sentences.zh: 故鑄自號慶湖遺老，有《慶湖遺老集》二十卷。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhu styled himself Old Survivor of Celebratory Lake; he had an Old Survivor of Celebratory Lake Collection in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Zhu styled himself Old Survivor of Celebratory Lake and left an Old Survivor of Celebratory Lake Collection in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 劉涇，字巨濟，簡州陽安人。

translations.literal: Liu Jing, styled Juji, was a man of Yang'an in Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jing, styled Juji, was a native of Yang'an in Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，王安石薦其才，召見，除經義所檢討。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination; Wang Anshi recommended his talent, he was summoned for an audience, and was appointed collating editor of the Institute for the Meaning of the Classics.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination. Wang Anshi recommended his talent, he was summoned for an audience, and was appointed collating editor of the Institute for the Meaning of the Classics.

sentences.zh: 久之，為太學博士，罷知咸陽縣，常州教授，通判莫州、成都府，除國子監丞，知處、虢、真、坊四州。

translations.literal: After some time he became Erudite of the Imperial Academy, then was dismissed and served as magistrate of Xianyang County, instructor at Changzhou, auxiliary prefect of Mozhou and Chengdu Prefecture, was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, and served as prefect of Chu, Guo, Zhen, and Fang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he became Erudite of the Imperial Academy. He was later dismissed and served as magistrate of Xianyang County, instructor at Changzhou, and auxiliary prefect of Mo Prefecture and Chengdu Prefecture. He was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and served as prefect of Chu, Guo, Zhen, and Fang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 元符末上書，召對，除職方郎中。

translations.literal: Late in Yuanfu he submitted a memorial, was summoned for a special audience, and was appointed Director in the Bureau of Military Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Yuanfu era he submitted a memorial, was summoned for a special audience, and was appointed Director in the Bureau of Military Appointments.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 涇為文務奇怪語，好進取，多為人排斥，屢躓不伸。

translations.literal: Jing wrote prose that strove for strange language, loved advancement, was often rejected by others, and repeatedly stumbled without fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: Jing wrote in a style that strove for strange language and loved advancement. He was often rejected by others and repeatedly stumbled without fulfilling his ambitions.

sentences.zh: 同時有鄭少微者，字明舉，成都人也，與涇俱以文知名，而仕不偶。

translations.literal: At the same time there was Zheng Shaowei, styled Mingju, a man of Chengdu, who with Jing was famed for writing, yet whose official career did not prosper.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there was Zheng Shaowei, styled Mingju, a native of Chengdu, who like Jing was famed for his writing, yet whose official career did not prosper.

sentences.zh: 鮑由，字欽止，處州龍泉人。

translations.literal: Bao You, styled Qinzhi, was a man of Longquan in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bao You, styled Qinzhi, was a native of Longquan in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 舉進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 嘗從王安石學，又親炙蘇軾，故其文汪洋閎肆，詩尤高妙。

translations.literal: He once studied under Wang Anshi and was also personally nurtured by Su Shi; therefore his prose was vast and expansive, and his poetry especially lofty and subtle.
translations.idiomatic: He had studied under Wang Anshi and was also personally nurtured by Su Shi. His prose was therefore vast and expansive, and his poetry especially lofty and subtle.

sentences.zh: 徽宗召對，除工部員外郎，居無何，以不合去，責監泗州轉般倉。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong summoned him for an audience and appointed him Vice Director in the Ministry of Works; after not long, because he did not fit in he left office and was assigned to supervise the transport depot at Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong summoned him for an audience and appointed him Vice Director in the Ministry of Works. Before long, because he did not fit in at court, he left office and was assigned to supervise the transport depot at Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 歷河東、福建路常平、廣西、淮南轉運判官，復召為郎。

translations.literal: He served successively as transport intendant of Hedong and Fujian circuits, transport vice commissioner of Guangxi and Huainan, and was again summoned as a court official.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as transport intendant of Hedong and Fujian circuits and as transport vice commissioner of Guangxi and Huainan, and was again summoned back to court as an official.

sentences.zh: 以言者罷，提點元封觀。

translations.literal: Because of critics he was dismissed and appointed intendant of Yuanfeng Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Because of critics he was dismissed and appointed intendant of Yuanfeng Abbey.

sentences.zh: 起知明州，又知海州，復奉祠。

translations.literal: He was reappointed prefect of Mingzhou, then prefect of Haizhou, and again received a sinecure stipend.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed prefect of Mingzhou and later prefect of Haizhou, and again received a sinecure stipend.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十六。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 嘗注杜甫詩，有文集五十卷。

translations.literal: He once annotated Du Fu's poetry and had a collected writings in fifty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He annotated Du Fu's poetry and left a collected writings in fifty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 黃伯思，字長睿，其遠祖自光州固始徙閩，為邵武人。

translations.literal: Huang Bosi, styled Changrui — his remote ancestor moved from Gushi in Guang Prefecture to Min and became a man of Shaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Bosi, styled Changrui, was descended from ancestors who had moved from Gushi in Guang Prefecture to Min; his family were natives of Shaowu.

sentences.zh: 祖履，資政殿大學士。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lu was a Grand Academician of the Hall for Assistance in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lu was a Grand Academician of the Hall for Assistance in Governance.

sentences.zh: 父應求，饒州司錄。

translations.literal: His father Yingqiu was Registrar of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yingqiu was Registrar of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 伯思體弱，如不勝衣，風韻灑落，飄飄有凌雲意。

translations.literal: Bosi's body was frail, as though unable to bear his clothes; his bearing was free and lofty, airy with the sense of soaring above the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Bosi was frail of body, as though his frame could barely support his clothes, yet his bearing was free and lofty, with an airy sense of soaring above the clouds.

sentences.zh: 自幼警敏，不好弄，日誦書千餘言。

translations.literal: From youth he was alert and keen, disliked play, and recited more than a thousand words of books each day.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was alert and keen, disliked play, and recited more than a thousand words from his books each day.

sentences.zh: 每聽履講經史，退與他兒言，無遺誤者。

translations.literal: Whenever he heard Lu lecture on the classics and histories, afterward when he spoke with other children there was nothing he forgot or got wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he heard Lu lecture on the classics and histories, he could afterward repeat everything to other children without a single omission or error.

sentences.zh: 嘗夢孔雀集於庭，覺而賦之，詞采甚麗。

translations.literal: He once dreamed that peacocks gathered in the courtyard; upon waking he composed a piece on it, its language very beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: He once dreamed that peacocks had gathered in the courtyard. Upon waking he composed a piece on the dream, and its language was very beautiful.

sentences.zh: 以履任為假承務郎。

translations.literal: Through Lu's office he received the provisional rank of Clerk for Official Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Through his grandfather Lu's office he received the provisional rank of Clerk for Official Affairs.

sentences.zh: 甫冠，入太學，校藝屢佔上游。

translations.literal: Just after coming of age he entered the Imperial Academy, and in competitive examinations repeatedly ranked at the top.
translations.idiomatic: Just after coming of age he entered the Imperial Academy, where in competitive examinations he repeatedly ranked at the top.

sentences.zh: 履將以恩例奏增秩，伯思固辭，履益奇之。

translations.literal: Lu intended to memorialize for an increase in rank under a privilege rule, but Bosi firmly declined; Lu admired him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Lu intended to memorialize for an increase in rank under a privilege rule, but Bosi firmly declined. Lu admired him all the more.

sentences.zh: 元符三年，進士高等，調磁州司法參軍，久不任，改通州司戶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfu he passed the jinshi examination with high rank, was assigned as judicial aide in Cizhou, long did not take up the post, and was transferred to be revenue clerk in Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanfu he passed the jinshi examination with high rank and was assigned as judicial aide in Cizhou. He long delayed taking up the post and was transferred to serve as revenue clerk in Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，服除，除河南府戶曹參軍，治劇不勞而辦。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother; when the mourning ended he was appointed revenue aide in Henan Prefecture, and in handling difficult affairs he accomplished them without strain.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother and completing the mourning period, he was appointed revenue aide in Henan Prefecture. Even in handling difficult affairs he accomplished them effortlessly.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，留守鄧洵武辟知右軍巡院。

translations.literal: When his term expired, the acting prefect Deng Xunwu recruited him to serve as director of the Right Army Patrolling Office.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired, the acting prefect Deng Xunwu recruited him to serve as director of the Right Army Patrolling Office.

sentences.zh: 伯思好古文奇字，洛下公卿家商、周、秦、漢彝器款識，研究字畫體制，悉能辨正是非，道其本末，遂以古文名家，凡字書討論備盡。

translations.literal: Bosi delighted in ancient script and unusual characters; in the homes of lords and ministers at Luoyang he studied the inscriptions on Shang, Zhou, Qin, and Han ritual vessels, researching the forms and structures of characters, all able to distinguish right from wrong and explain their origins and ends — thereby becoming a master of ancient script; in all discussions of character books he was thoroughly complete.
translations.idiomatic: Bosi loved ancient script and unusual characters. He studied the inscriptions on Shang, Zhou, Qin, and Han ritual vessels in the homes of Luoyang's nobles, mastering the forms and structures of characters until he could judge authenticity, explain origins, and became a leading authority on paleography. His discussions of character books were exhaustive.

sentences.zh: 初，淳化中博求古法書，命待詔王著續正法帖，伯思病其乖偽龐雜，考引載籍，鹹有依據，作《刊誤》二卷。

translations.literal: At first, in the Chunhua period a broad search was made for ancient model calligraphy, and Attendant Drafter Wang Zhu was ordered to continue the Correct Model Albums; Bosi found fault with their perversity, falsity, and chaotic mass, examined and cited transmitted records — all had basis — and wrote Corrections in two juan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua reign a broad search was made for ancient model calligraphy, and Attendant Drafter Wang Zhu was ordered to continue the Correct Model Albums. Bosi found them riddled with errors, forgeries, and clutter. Citing transmitted records with solid evidence, he wrote Corrections in two juan.

sentences.zh: 由是篆、隸、正、行、草、章草、飛白皆至妙絕，得其尺牘者，多藏□。

translations.literal: Thereby seal script, clerical script, regular script, running script, cursive script, draft cursive, and flying-white all reached utmost excellence; those who obtained his letters mostly treasured them [lacuna].
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter his seal script, clerical script, regular script, running script, cursive script, draft cursive, and flying-white calligraphy all reached consummate mastery. Those who obtained his letters treasured them closely.

sentences.zh: 又二年，除詳定《九域圖志》所編修官兼《六典》檢閱文字，改京秩。

translations.literal: After another two years, he was appointed Compiler-Reviewer for the Detailed Determination of the Territorial Gazetteer in Nine Regions and concurrently Text Reviewer for the Six Institutions, and was changed to capital rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was appointed compiler-reviewer for the Detailed Territorial Gazetteer in Nine Regions and concurrent text reviewer for the Six Institutions, and was promoted to capital rank.

sentences.zh: 尋監護崇恩太后園陵使司，掌管箋奏。

translations.literal: Shortly he supervised the Office of the Commissioner for the Park Tomb of Empress Dowager Chong'en, managing memorials and reports.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he supervised the office overseeing the park tomb of Empress Dowager Chong'en, managing memorials and reports.

sentences.zh: 以修書恩，升朝列，擢秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: Through grace for compiling books, he rose to the court ranks and was promoted to Collator of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: For his work on book compilation he was raised to court rank and promoted to Collator of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷秘書郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 縱觀冊府藏書，至忘寢食，自《六經》及歷代史書、諸子百家、天官地理、律歷卜筮之說無不精詣。

translations.literal: He roamed through the archive collections until forgetting sleep and food; from the Six Classics to historical books of successive ages, the hundred schools, celestial offices, geography, pitch pipes, calendars, and divination — none he did not master with precision.
translations.idiomatic: He ranged through the imperial archives until he forgot to eat or sleep. From the Six Classics to dynastic histories, the hundred schools, astronomy, geography, music, calendrics, and divination — there was no field he did not master.

sentences.zh: 凡詔講明前世典章文物、集古器考定真贗，以素學與聞，議論發明居多，館閣諸公自以為不及也。

translations.literal: Whenever edicts explained the institutions and artifacts of former ages, or gathered antiquities to determine authenticity, with his lifelong learning he took part — in discourse and invention he mostly led, and the gentlemen of the academies considered themselves not equal.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court was ordered to clarify the institutions and artifacts of earlier ages, or to assemble antiquities and judge authenticity, Bosi was consulted for his lifelong learning. His explanations usually led the discussion, and the academy's senior scholars acknowledged they could not match him.

sentences.zh: 逾再考，丁外艱，宿抱羸瘵，因喪尤甚。

translations.literal: After more than two examinations, he entered mourning for his father; long he had carried a wasting illness, and because of the mourning it was all the worse.
translations.idiomatic: After more than two rounds of evaluation he entered mourning for his father. He had long suffered from a wasting illness, and the mourning made it far worse.

sentences.zh: 服除，復舊職。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he resumed his former post.

sentences.zh: 伯思頗好道家，自號雲林子，別字霄賓。

translations.literal: Bosi was rather fond of Daoism, styled himself Master of Cloud Forest, and took the alternative name Guest of the Azure Sky.
translations.idiomatic: Bosi was drawn to Daoism, styled himself Master of Cloud Forest, and took the alternative name Guest of the Azure Sky.

sentences.zh: 及至京，夢人告曰：「子非久人間，上帝有命典司文翰。」

translations.literal: When he reached the capital, a man in a dream told him: "You will not long remain among men; the Supreme Lord has ordered you to preside over literary records."
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital, someone told him in a dream, "You will not long remain in the world of men. The Supreme Lord has appointed you to preside over literary records."

sentences.zh: 覺而書之。

translations.literal: On waking he wrote it down.
translations.idiomatic: On waking he wrote it down.

sentences.zh: 不逾月，以政和八年卒，年四十。

translations.literal: Within a month, in the eighth year of Zhenghe he died, age forty.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he died in the eighth year of Zhenghe, at the age of forty.

sentences.zh: 伯思學問慕揚雄，詩慕李白，文慕柳宗元。

translations.literal: In learning Bosi admired Yang Xiong, in poetry Li Bai, in prose Liu Zongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In scholarship he admired Yang Xiong, in poetry Li Bai, and in prose Liu Zongyuan.

sentences.zh: 有文集五十卷、《翼騷》一卷。

translations.literal: He had a collection of writings in fifty juan and Wings to the Lisao in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collection of writings in fifty juan and Wings to the Lisao in one juan.

sentences.zh: 二子：詔，右宣教郎、荊湖南路安撫司書寫機宜文字；

translations.literal: Two sons: Zhao, Right Instructor and Drafting Secretary for Military Affairs on the Jinghu South circuit Pacification Commission;
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Zhao, Right Instructor and drafting secretary for military affairs on the Jinghu South Pacification Commission;

sentences.zh: 言乃，右從事郎、福州懷安尉，裒伯思平日議論題跋為《東觀余論》三卷。

translations.literal: Yannai, Right Attendant and Assistant Magistrate of Huai'an in Fuzhou — gathered Bosi's daily discourses and colophons into Eastern Observatory Remaining Discussions in three juan.
translations.idiomatic: and Yannai, Right Attendant and Assistant Magistrate of Huai'an in Fuzhou, who gathered Bosi's daily commentaries and colophons into Eastern Observatory Remaining Discussions in three juan.
